# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: basic Basic authentication, with the user's email as the username, and the API
key as the password. The API key can be fetched using the
`/fetch_api_key` or `/dev_fetch_api_key` endpoints.

<h1 id="zulip-rest-api-authentication">authentication</h1>

## Fetch an API key (production)

<a id="opIdfetch-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/fetch_api_key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'username=iago%40zulip.com&password=abcd1234'
```

`POST /fetch_api_key`

This API endpoint is used by clients such as the Zulip mobile and
terminal apps to implement password-based authentication. Given the
user's Zulip login credentials, it returns a Zulip API key that the client
can use to make requests as the user.

This endpoint is only useful for Zulip servers/organizations with
EmailAuthBackend or LDAPAuthBackend enabled.

The Zulip mobile apps also support SSO/social authentication (GitHub
auth, Google auth, SAML, etc.) that does not use this endpoint. Instead,
the mobile apps reuse the web login flow passing the `mobile_flow_otp` in
a webview, and the credentials are returned to the app (encrypted) via a redirect
to a `zulip://` URL.

!!! warn ""

    **Note:** If you signed up using passwordless authentication and
    never had a password, you can [reset your password](/help/change-your-password).

See the [API keys](/api/api-keys) documentation for more details
on how to download an API key manually.

In a [Zulip development environment](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/overview.html),
see also [the unauthenticated variant](/api/dev-fetch-api-key).


> Body parameter

```yaml
username: iago@zulip.com
password: abcd1234
```

<h3 id="fetch-an-api-key-production-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» username|body|string|true|The username to be used for authentication (typically, the email<br>address, but depending on configuration, it could be an LDAP username).<br><br>See the `require_email_format_usernames` parameter documented in<br>[GET /server_settings](/api/get-server-settings) for details.<br>|
|» password|body|string|true|The user's Zulip password (or LDAP password, if LDAP authentication is in use).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "api_key": "gjA04ZYcqXKalvYMA8OeXSfzUOLrtbZv",
  "email": "iago@zulip.com",
  "user_id": 5
}
```

<h3 id="fetch-an-api-key-production-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Valid credentials the client can use to access the Zulip API:<br>|[ApiKeyResponse](#schemaapikeyresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Fetch an API key (JWT)

<a id="opIdjwt-fetch-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/jwt/fetch_api_key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJlbWFpbCI6ImhhbWxldEB6dWxpcC5jb20ifQ.EsHxSVt54zPR-ywgPH54TB1FYmrGKsfq7hsQEhp_9w0&include_profile=false'
```

`POST /jwt/fetch_api_key`

This API endpoint is used by clients to implement JSON Web Token
(JWT) authentication. Given a JWT identifying a Zulip user, it
returns a Zulip API key that the client can use to make requests
as the user.

!!! warn ""

    **Note:** This endpoint is only useful for Zulip servers/organizations
    with [JSON web token authentication][prod-jwt-auth] enabled.

See the [API keys](/api/api-keys) documentation for more details
on how to manage API keys manually.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 7.0 (feature level 160).

[prod-jwt-auth]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/authentication-methods.html#json-web-tokens-jwt


> Body parameter

```yaml
token: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJlbWFpbCI6ImhhbWxldEB6dWxpcC5jb20ifQ.EsHxSVt54zPR-ywgPH54TB1FYmrGKsfq7hsQEhp_9w0
include_profile: false
```

<h3 id="fetch-an-api-key-jwt-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» token|body|string|true|A JSON Web Token for the target user.<br><br>The token payload must contain a custom `email` claim with the target<br>user's email address, e.g., `{"email": "<target user email>"}`.<br>|
|» include_profile|body|boolean|false|Whether to include a `user` object containing the target<br>user's profile details in the response.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "api_key": "gjA04ZYcqXKalvYMA8OeXSfzUOLrtbZv",
  "email": "hamlet@zulip.com"
}
```

<h3 id="fetch-an-api-key-jwt-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|

<h3 id="fetch-an-api-key-jwt-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|msg|string|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|[IgnoredParametersUnsupported](#schemaignoredparametersunsupported)|false|none|An array of any parameters sent in the request that are not<br>supported by the endpoint.<br><br>See [error handling](/api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters) documentation<br>for details on this and its change history.<br>|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|msg|object|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|object|false|none|none|
|api_key|string|true|none|The API key that can be used to authenticate as the requested user.<br>|
|email|string|true|none|The email address of the user who owns the API key.<br>|
|user|object|false|none|Only present if `include_profile` parameter was set to `true`.<br><br>A dictionary with data on the target user.<br>|
|» user_id|integer|false|none|The unique ID of the user.<br>|
|» delivery_email|string \| null|false|none|The user's real email address. This value will be `null` if you cannot<br>access user's real email address. For bot users, this field is always<br>set to the real email of the bot, because bot users always have<br>`email_address_visibility` set to everyone.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 7.0 (feature level 163), this field was<br>present only when `email_address_visibility` was restricted and you had<br>access to the user's real email. As of this feature level, this field<br>is always present, including the case when `email_address_visibility`<br>is set to everyone (and therefore not restricted).<br>|
|» email|string|false|none|The Zulip API email address of the user or bot.<br><br>If you do not have permission to view the email address of the target user,<br>this will be a fake email address that is usable for the Zulip API but nothing else.<br>|

For users imported from other<br>applications and users created via the API, this is set to the<br>account creation time until the user logs in for the first time,<br>after which it is updated to that login time.<br><br>For imported users, clients can use the `is_imported_stub` flag<br>to determine how to display this field: when `is_imported_stub`<br>is `true`, the user has not yet logged in and this value is the<br>account creation time during import; when `is_imported_stub` is<br>`false`, this value reflects when the user first logged in.<br><br>**Changes**: Starting with Zulip 12.0 (feature level 475),<br>this field is updated when an imported stub user or a user created<br>via the API logs in for the first time.<br>|
|» is_active|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user account has been deactivated.<br>|

|» is_admin|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user is an organization administrator.<br>|
|» is_guest|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user is a guest user.<br>|
|» is_bot|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user is a bot or full account.<br>|
|» bot_type|integer \| null|false|none|An integer describing the type of bot:<br><br>- `null` if the user isn't a bot.<br>- `1` for a `Generic` bot.<br>- `2` for an `Incoming webhook` bot.<br>- `3` for an `Outgoing webhook` bot.<br>- `4` for an `Embedded` bot.<br>|
|» bot_owner_id|integer \| null|false|none|If the user is a bot (i.e. `is_bot` is true), then `bot_owner_id`<br>is the user ID of the bot's owner (usually, whoever created the bot).<br><br>Will be `null` for legacy bots that do not have an owner.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). In previous<br>versions, there was a `bot_owner` field containing the email<br>address of the bot's owner.<br>|
|» role|integer|false|none|[Organization-level role](/api/roles-and-permissions) of the user.<br>Possible values are:<br><br>- 100 = Organization owner<br>- 200 = Organization administrator<br>- 300 = Organization moderator<br>- 400 = Member<br>- 600 = Guest<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 59).<br>|
|» timezone|string|false|none|The IANA identifier of the user's [profile time zone](/help/change-your-timezone),<br>which is used primarily to display the user's local time to other users.<br>|

Stub accounts are used to represent the senders<br>for imported messages. Stub accounts can be converted to regular Zulip<br>accounts when the user starts using Zulip, preserving that imported<br>user's message history.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 433).<br>|

## Fetch an API key (development only)

<a id="opIddev-fetch-api-key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/dev_fetch_api_key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'username=iago%40zulip.com'
```

`POST /dev_fetch_api_key`

For easy testing of mobile apps and other clients and against Zulip
development servers, we support fetching a Zulip API key for any user
on the development server without authentication (so that they can
implement analogues of the one-click login process available for Zulip
development servers on the web).

!!! warn ""

    **Note:** This endpoint is only available on Zulip development
    servers; for obvious security reasons it will always return an error
    in a Zulip production server.


> Body parameter

```yaml
username: iago@zulip.com
```

<h3 id="fetch-an-api-key-development-only-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» username|body|string|true|The email address for the user that owns the API key.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "api_key": "gjA04ZYcqXKalvYMA8OeXSfzUOLrtbZv",
  "email": "iago@zulip.com",
  "user_id": 5
}
```

<h3 id="fetch-an-api-key-development-only-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|[ApiKeyResponse](#schemaapikeyresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## List users (development only)

<a id="opIddev-list-users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/dev_list_users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /dev_list_users`

Get a list of all, non-bot users in a [Zulip development
server](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/overview.html).
This endpoint is used by mobile developers to fetch users for the
development login flow.

!!! warn ""

    **Note:** This endpoint is only available on Zulip development
    servers; for obvious security reasons it will always return an error
    in a Zulip production server.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "direct_admins": [
    {
      "email": "iago@zulip.com",
      "realm_url": "http://localhost:9991"
    }
  ],
  "direct_users": [
    {
      "email": "hamlet@zulip.com",
      "realm_url": "http://localhost:9991"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-users-development-only-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|

<h3 id="list-users-development-only-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|msg|string|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|[IgnoredParametersUnsupported](#schemaignoredparametersunsupported)|false|none|An array of any parameters sent in the request that are not<br>supported by the endpoint.<br><br>See [error handling](/api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters) documentation<br>for details on this and its change history.<br>|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|msg|object|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|object|false|none|none|
|direct_admins|[object]|false|none|A list of administrators in the development server.<br>|
|» email|string|false|none|The email of the dev admin user.<br>|
|» realm_url|string|false|none|The URL of the dev admin user's organization.<br>|
|direct_users|[object]|false|none|A list of non-admin users in the development server.<br>|
|» email|string|false|none|The email of the dev user.<br>|
|» realm_url|string|false|none|The URL of the dev user's organization.<br>|

This operation does not require authentication

<h1 id="zulip-rest-api-realtimeevents">real_time_events</h1>

## Get events from an event queue

<a id="opIdget-events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/events?queue_id=fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /events`

This endpoint allows you to receive new events from
[a registered event queue](/api/register-queue).

Long-lived clients should use the
`event_queue_longpoll_timeout_seconds` property returned by
`POST /register` as the client-side HTTP request timeout for
calls to this endpoint. It is guaranteed to be higher than
heartbeat timeout and should be respected by clients to
avoid breaking when heartbeat timeout increases.


<h3 id="get-events-from-an-event-queue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|queue_id|query|string|true|The ID of an event queue that was previously registered via<br>`POST /api/v1/register` (see [Register a queue](/api/register-queue)).<br>|
|last_event_id|query|integer|false|The highest event ID in this queue that you've received and<br>wish to acknowledge. See the [code for<br>`call_on_each_event`](https://github.com/zulip/python-zulip-api/blob/main/zulip/zulip/__init__.py)<br>in the [zulip Python<br>module](https://github.com/zulip/python-zulip-api) for an<br>example implementation of correctly processing each event<br>exactly once.<br>|
|dont_block|query|boolean|false|Set to `true` if the client is requesting a nonblocking reply. If not<br>specified, the request will block until either a new event is available<br>or a few minutes have passed, in which case the server will send the<br>client a heartbeat event.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "queue_id": "fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8",
  "events": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "message": {
        "avatar_url": "https://url/for/othello-bots/avatar",
        "client": "website",
        "content": "I come not, friends, to steal away your hearts.",
        "content_type": "text/x-markdown",
        "display_recipient": "Denmark",
        "id": 12345678,
        "recipient_id": 12314,
        "sender_email": "othello-bot@example.com",
        "sender_full_name": "Othello Bot",
        "sender_id": 13215,
        "sender_realm_str": "example",
        "topic_links": [],
        "timestamp": 1375978403,
        "type": "stream"
      },
      "type": "message"
    },
    {
      "id": 1,
      "message": {
        "avatar_url": "https://url/for/othello-bots/avatar",
        "client": "website",
        "content": "With mirth and laughter let old wrinkles come.",
        "content_type": "text/x-markdown",
        "display_recipient": [
          {
            "email": "hamlet@example.com",
            "full_name": "Hamlet of Denmark",
            "id": 31572
          }
        ],
        "id": 12345679,
        "recipient_id": 18391,
        "sender_email": "othello-bot@example.com",
        "sender_full_name": "Othello Bot",
        "sender_id": 13215,
        "sender_realm_str": "example",
        "subject": "",
        "topic_links": [],
        "timestamp": 1375978404,
        "type": "private"
      },
      "type": "message"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Bad event queue ID: fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8",
  "code": "BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID",
  "queue_id": "fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8"
}
```

<h3 id="get-events-from-an-event-queue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-events-from-an-event-queue-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

## Delete an event queue

<a id="opIddelete-queue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/events \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'queue_id=fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8'
```

`DELETE /events`

Delete a previously registered queue.


> Body parameter

```yaml
queue_id: fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8
```

<h3 id="delete-an-event-queue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» queue_id|body|string|true|The ID of an event queue that was previously registered via<br>`POST /api/v1/register` (see [Register a queue](/api/register-queue)).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Bad event queue ID: fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8",
  "code": "BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID",
  "queue_id": "fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-event-queue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|[JsonSuccess](#schemajsonsuccess)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

## Register an event queue

<a id="opIdregister-queue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/register \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'apply_markdown=true&client_gravatar=false&include_subscribers=true&slim_presence=true&presence_history_limit_days=365&event_types=%5B%22message%22%5D&all_public_streams=true&client_capabilities=%7B%22notification_settings_null%22%3Atrue%7D&fetch_event_types=%5B%22message%22%5D&narrow=%5B%5B%22channel%22%2C%22Denmark%22%5D%5D&idle_queue_timeout=3600'
```

`POST /register`

This powerful endpoint can be used to register a Zulip "event queue"
(subscribed to certain types of "events", or updates to the messages
and other Zulip data the current user has access to), as well as to
fetch the current state of that data.

(`register` also powers the `call_on_each_event` Python API, and is
intended primarily for complex applications for which the more convenient
`call_on_each_event` API is insufficient).

This endpoint returns a `queue_id` and a `last_event_id`; these can be
used in subsequent calls to the
["events" endpoint](/api/get-events) to request events from
the Zulip server using long-polling.

The server will queue events for up to `idle_queue_timeout_secs`
seconds of inactivity. After that timeout, your event queue will be
garbage-collected. The server will send `heartbeat` events
every minute, which makes it easy to implement a robust client that
does not miss events unless the client loses network connectivity
with the Zulip server for longer than the configured timeout.

Once the server garbage-collects your event queue, the server will
[return an error](/api/get-events#bad_event_queue_id-errors)
with a code of `BAD_EVENT_QUEUE_ID` if you try to fetch events from
the event queue. Your software will need to handle that error
condition by re-initializing itself (e.g. this is what triggers your
browser reloading the Zulip web app when your laptop comes back online
after being offline for more than `idle_queue_timeout_secs` seconds).

When prototyping with this API, we recommend first calling `register`
with no `event_types` parameter to see all the available data from all
supported event types. Before using your client in production, you
should set appropriate `event_types` and `fetch_event_types` filters
so that your client only requests the data it needs. A few minutes
doing this often saves 90% of the total bandwidth and other resources
consumed by a client using this API.

See the [events system developer documentation][events-system-docs]
if you need deeper details about how the Zulip event queue system
works, avoids clients needing to worry about large classes of
potentially messy races, etc.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 481),
the `idle_queue_timeout` request parameter and `idle_queue_timeout_secs`
response field were added to allow clients to configure
how long the server keeps an event queue alive during inactivity.

Removed `dense_mode` setting in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 364)
as we now have `web_font_size_px` and `web_line_height_percent`
settings for more control.

Before Zulip 7.0 (feature level 183), the
`realm_community_topic_editing_limit_seconds` property
was returned by the response. It was removed because it
had not been in use since the realm setting
`move_messages_within_stream_limit_seconds` was introduced
in feature level 162.

In Zulip 7.0 (feature level 163), the realm setting
`email_address_visibility` was removed. It was replaced by a [user
setting](/api/update-settings#parameter-email_address_visibility) with
a [realm user default][user-defaults], with the encoding of different
values preserved. Clients can support all versions by supporting the
current API and treating every user as having the realm's
`email_address_visibility` value.

[user-defaults]: /api/update-realm-user-settings-defaults#parameter-email_address_visibility
[events-system-docs]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/events-system.html


> Body parameter

```yaml
apply_markdown: true
client_gravatar: false
include_subscribers: "true"
slim_presence: true
presence_history_limit_days: 365
event_types:
  - message
all_public_streams: true
client_capabilities:
  notification_settings_null: true
fetch_event_types:
  - message
narrow:
  -
    - channel
    - Denmark
idle_queue_timeout: 3600
```

<h3 id="register-an-event-queue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» apply_markdown|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` if you would like the content to be rendered in HTML<br>format (otherwise the API will return the raw text that the user<br>entered)<br>|
|» client_gravatar|body|boolean|false|Whether the client supports computing gravatars URLs. If<br>enabled, `avatar_url` will be included in the response only<br>if there is a Zulip avatar, and will be `null` for users who<br>are using gravatar as their avatar. This option<br>significantly reduces the compressed size of user data,<br>since gravatar URLs are long, random strings and thus do not<br>compress well. The `client_gravatar` field is set to `true` if<br>clients can compute their own gravatars.<br><br>The default value is `true` for authenticated requests and<br>`false` for [unauthenticated<br>requests](/help/public-access-option). Passing `true` in<br>an unauthenticated request is an error.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 6.0 (feature level 149), this<br>parameter was silently ignored and processed as though it<br>were `false` in unauthenticated requests.<br>|
|» include_subscribers|body|string|false|Whether each returned channel object should include a `subscribers`<br>field containing a list of the user IDs of its subscribers.<br><br>Client apps supporting organizations with many thousands of users<br>should not pass `true`, because the full subscriber matrix may be<br>several megabytes of data. The `partial` value, combined with the<br>`subscriber_count` and fetching subscribers for individual channels as<br>needed, is recommended to support client app features where channel<br>subscriber data is useful.<br><br>If a client passes `partial` for this parameter, the server may,<br>for some channels, return a subset of the channel's subscribers<br>in the `partial_subscribers` field instead of the `subscribers` field,<br>which always contains the complete set of subscribers.<br><br>The server guarantees that it will always return a `subscribers`<br>field for channels with fewer than 250 total subscribers. When<br>returning a `partial_subscribers` field, the server guarantees<br>that all bot users and users active within the last 14 days will<br>be included. For other cases, the server may use its discretion<br>to determine which channels and users to include, balancing between<br>payload size and usefulness of the data provided to the client.<br><br>Passing `true` in an [unauthenticated<br>request](/help/public-access-option) is an error.<br><br>**Changes**: The `partial` value is new in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 412).<br><br>Before Zulip 6.0 (feature level 149), this parameter was silently<br>ignored and processed as though it were `false` in unauthenticated<br>requests.<br><br>New in Zulip 2.1.0.<br>|
|» slim_presence|body|boolean|false|If `true`, the `presences` object returned in the response will be keyed<br>by user ID and the entry for each user's presence data will be in the<br>modern format.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (no feature level; API unstable).<br>|
|» presence_history_limit_days|body|integer|false|Limits how far back in time to fetch user presence data. If not specified,<br>defaults to 14 days. A value of N means that the oldest presence data<br>fetched will be from at most N days ago.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 288).<br>|
|» event_types|body|[Event_types](#schemaevent_types)|false|A JSON-encoded array indicating which types of events you're interested<br>in. Values that you might find useful include:<br><br>- **message** (messages)<br>- **subscription** (changes in your subscriptions)<br>- **realm_user** (changes to users in the organization and<br>  their properties, such as their name).<br><br>If you do not specify this parameter, you will receive all<br>events, and have to filter out the events not relevant to<br>your client in your client code. For most applications, one<br>is only interested in messages, so one specifies:<br>`"event_types": ["message"]`<br><br>Event types not supported by the server are ignored, in order to simplify<br>the implementation of client apps that support multiple server versions.<br>|
|» all_public_streams|body|[AllPublicChannels](#schemaallpublicchannels)|false|Whether you would like to request message events from all public<br>channels. Useful for workflow bots that you'd like to see all new messages<br>sent to public channels. (You can also subscribe the user to private channels).<br>|
|» client_capabilities|body|object|false|Dictionary containing details on features the client supports that are<br>relevant to the format of responses sent by the server.<br><br>- `notification_settings_null`: Boolean for whether the<br>  client can handle the current API with `null` values for<br>  channel-level notification settings (which means the channel<br>  is not customized and should inherit the user's global<br>  notification settings for channel messages).<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 2.1.0. In earlier Zulip releases,<br>  channel-level notification settings were simple booleans.<br><br>- `bulk_message_deletion`: Boolean for whether the client's<br>  handler for the `delete_message` event type has been<br>  updated to process the new bulk format (with a<br>  `message_ids`, rather than a singleton `message_id`).<br>  Otherwise, the server will send `delete_message` events<br>  in a loop.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 13). This<br>  capability is for backwards-compatibility; it will be<br>  required in a future server release.<br><br>- `user_avatar_url_field_optional`: Boolean for whether the<br>  client required avatar URLs for all users, or supports<br>  using `GET /avatar/{user_id}` to access user avatars. If the<br>  client has this capability, the server may skip sending a<br>  `avatar_url` field in the `realm_user` at its sole discretion<br>  to optimize network performance. This is an important optimization<br>  in organizations with 10,000s of users.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 18).<br><br>- `stream_typing_notifications`: Boolean for whether the client<br>  supports channel typing notifications.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 58). This capability is<br>  for backwards-compatibility; it will be required in a<br>  future server release.<br><br>- `user_settings_object`: Has no effect with modern servers. Previously,<br>  this was a boolean for whether the client supported the modern<br>  [`user_settings` event type](/api/get-events#user_settings-update) and<br>  the top-level `user_settings` object in this endpoint's response.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: Prior to Zulip 12.0 (feature level 439), if false, the<br>  server would additionally send the legacy `update_global_notifications`<br>  and `update_display_settings` event types, if requested.<br>  <br /><br>  New in Zulip 5.0 (feature level 89). Because the feature level 89 API<br>  changes were merged together, clients could safely make a request with<br>  this client capability, and also request all three event types<br>  (`user_settings`, `update_display_settings`, and<br>  `update_global_notifications`), and then use the `zulip_feature_level`<br>  in this endpoint's response or the presence/absence of a `user_settings`<br>  key to determine where to look for the data.<br><br>- `linkifier_url_template`: Boolean for whether the client accepts<br>  [linkifiers][help-linkifiers] that use [RFC 6570][rfc6570] compliant<br>  URL templates for linkifying matches. If false or unset, then the<br>  `realm_linkifiers` array in the `/register` response will be empty<br>  if present, and no `realm_linkifiers` [events][events-linkifiers]<br>  will be sent to the client.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 7.0 (feature level 176). This capability<br>  is for backwards-compatibility.<br><br>- `user_list_incomplete`: Boolean for whether the client supports not having an<br>  incomplete user database. If true, then the `realm_users` array in the `register`<br>  response will not include data for inaccessible users and clients of guest users will<br>  not receive `realm_user op:add` events for newly created users that are not accessible<br>  to the current user.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 232). This<br>  capability is for backwards-compatibility.<br><br>- `include_deactivated_groups`: Boolean for whether the client can handle<br>  deactivated user groups by themselves. If false, then the `realm_user_groups`<br>  array in the `/register` response will only include active groups, and clients<br>  will receive a `remove` event instead of an `update` event when a group is<br>  deactivated, and an `add` event instead of an `update` event when a group is<br>  reactivated. Additionally, when a deactivated user group is renamed, no<br>  `update` event is sent to the client. Other `update` events for a<br>  deactivated group, such as changes to its description and permission<br>  settings, are still sent.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 294). This<br>  capability is for backwards-compatibility.<br><br>- `archived_channels`: Boolean for whether the client supports processing<br>  [archived channels](/help/archive-a-channel) in the `stream` and<br>  `subscription` event types. If `false`, the server will not include data<br>  related to archived channels in the `register` response or in events.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 315). This allows clients to<br>  access archived channels, without breaking backwards-compatibility for<br>  existing clients.<br><br>- `empty_topic_name`: Boolean for whether the client supports processing<br>  the empty string as a topic name. Clients not declaring this capability<br>  will be sent the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name` found in the<br>  [POST /register](/api/register-queue) response instead of the empty string<br>  wherever topic names appear in the register response or events involving<br>  topic names.<br>  <br/><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334). Previously,<br>  the empty string was not a valid topic name.<br><br>- `simplified_presence_events`: Boolean for whether the client supports<br>  receiving the [`presence` event type](/api/get-events#presence) with<br>  user presence data in the modern format. If true, the server will<br>  send these events with the `presences` field that has the user presence<br>  data in the modern format. Otherwise, these event will contain fields<br>  with legacy format user presence data.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 419).<br><br>- `individual_emoji_changes`: Boolean for whether the client supports<br>  receiving the [`realm_emoji/add` and `realm_emoji/edit` event<br>  types](/api/get-events#realm_emoji-add). If true, the server will<br>  send individual `realm_emoji/add` events when a custom emoji is<br>  added, and `realm_emoji/edit` events when a custom emoji's<br>  properties are changed (e.g., deactivated). Otherwise, the server<br>  will send the legacy `realm_emoji/update` event containing all<br>  custom emoji for the organization.<br>  <br /><br>  **Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 491).<br><br>[help-linkifiers]: /help/add-a-custom-linkifier<br>[rfc6570]: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570.html<br>[events-linkifiers]: /api/get-events#realm_linkifiers<br>|
|» fetch_event_types|body|[string]|false|Same as the `event_types` parameter except that the values in<br>`fetch_event_types` are used to fetch initial data. If<br>`fetch_event_types` is not provided, `event_types` is used and if<br>`event_types` is not provided, this parameter defaults to `null`.<br><br>Event types not supported by the server are ignored, in order to simplify<br>the implementation of client apps that support multiple server versions.<br>|
|» narrow|body|[Narrow](#schemanarrow)|false|A JSON-encoded array of arrays of length 2 indicating the<br>[narrow filter(s)](/api/construct-narrow) for which you'd<br>like to receive events for.<br><br>For example, to receive events for direct messages (including<br>group direct messages) received by the user, one can use<br>`"narrow": [["is", "dm"]]`.<br><br>Unlike the API for [fetching messages](/api/get-messages),<br>this narrow parameter is simply a filter on messages that the<br>user receives through their channel subscriptions (or because<br>they are a recipient of a direct message).<br><br>This means that a client that requests a `narrow` filter of<br>`[["channel", "Denmark"]]` will receive events for new messages<br>sent to that channel while the user is subscribed to that<br>channel. The client will not receive any message events at all<br>if the user is not subscribed to `"Denmark"`.<br><br>Newly created bot users are not usually subscribed to any<br>channels, so bots using this API need to be<br>[subscribed](/api/subscribe) to any channels whose messages<br>you'd like them to process using this endpoint.<br><br>See the `all_public_streams` parameter for how to process all<br>public channel messages in an organization.<br><br>**Changes**: See [changes section](/api/construct-narrow#changes)<br>of search/narrow filter documentation.<br>|
|» idle_queue_timeout|body|integer \| string|false|At least how long (in seconds) the server should keep the event<br>queue alive when the client is not polling. If the client does<br>not poll before this timeout, the queue will eventually be<br>garbage-collected.<br><br>Alternatively, the string `"mobile"` can be passed to use the<br>server's recommended timeout for mobile clients. This is<br>currently 12 hours, but may change in the future.<br><br>If not specified, the server uses a default of 10 minutes. The<br>maximum allowed value is 7 days.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 481).<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|

This order can be modified with [`PATCH<br>/realm/linkifiers`](/api/reorder-linkifiers).<br><br>Clients will receive an empty array unless the event queue is<br>registered with the client capability `{"linkifier_url_template": true}`.<br>See [`client_capabilities`](/api/register-queue#parameter-client_capabilities)<br>parameter for how this can be specified.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 7.0 (feature level 176), the<br>`linkifier_url_template` client capability was not required. The<br>requirement was added because linkifiers were updated to contain<br>a URL template instead of a URL format string, which was a not<br>backwards-compatible change.<br><br>New in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 54). Clients can access this data for<br>servers on earlier feature levels via the legacy `realm_filters` property.<br>|

This replaced `url_format`,<br>which contained a URL format string.<br>|
|» id|integer|false|none|The ID of the linkifier.<br>|
|realm_filters|[[integer \| string]]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Legacy property for [linkifiers](/help/add-a-custom-linkifier).<br>Present if `realm_filters` is present in `fetch_event_types`.<br><br>When present, this is always an empty array.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 7.0 (feature level 176), this was<br>an array of tuples, where each tuple described a linkifier. The first<br>element of the tuple was a string regex pattern which represented the<br>pattern to be linkified on matching, for example `"#(?P<id>[123])"`.<br>The second element was a URL format string that the pattern should be<br>linkified with. A URL format string for the above example would be<br>`"https://realm.com/my_realm_filter/%(id)s"`. And the third element<br>was the ID of the realm filter.<br><br>**Deprecated** in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 54), replaced by the<br>`realm_linkifiers` key.<br>|

Otherwise,<br>it will only include bots owned by the user (either because the user created<br>the bot or an administrator transferred the bot's ownership to the user).<br><br>**Changes**: Removed `avatar_url`, `bot_type`, `email`, `full_name`, `is_active`<br>and `owner_id` fields from the dictionary in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 474).<br>Clients can get all these data from the corresponding user object.<br><br>Removed `api_key` field from the dictionary in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 474).<br>Clients now use [`GET /bots/{bot_id}/api_key`](/api/get-bot-api-key)<br>to get api key for the bot.<br>|

|server_emoji_data_url|string|false|none|Present if `realm` is present in `fetch_event_types`.<br><br>The URL to a JSON file that describes which emoji names map to which<br>emoji codes, for all Unicode emoji this Zulip server accepts.<br><br>The data at the given URL is a JSON object with one property, `code_to_names`.<br>The value of that property is a JSON object where each key is an<br>[emoji code](/api/add-reaction#parameter-emoji_code) for an available<br>Unicode emoji, and each value is the corresponding<br>[emoji names](/api/add-reaction#parameter-emoji_name) for this emoji,<br>with the canonical name for the emoji always appearing first.<br><br>The HTTP response at that URL will have appropriate HTTP caching headers, such<br>any HTTP implementation should get a cached version if emoji haven't changed<br>since the last request.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 140).<br>|

## post/real-time

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/real-time \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'event_types=%5B%22message%22%5D&narrow=%5B%5B%22channel%22%2C%22Denmark%22%5D%5D&all_public_streams=true'
```

`POST /real-time`

(Ignored)


> Body parameter

```yaml
event_types:
  - message
narrow:
  -
    - channel
    - Denmark
all_public_streams: true
```

<h3 id="postreal-time-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» event_types|body|[Event_types](#schemaevent_types)|false|A JSON-encoded array indicating which types of events you're interested<br>in. Values that you might find useful include:<br><br>- **message** (messages)<br>- **subscription** (changes in your subscriptions)<br>- **realm_user** (changes to users in the organization and<br>  their properties, such as their name).<br><br>If you do not specify this parameter, you will receive all<br>events, and have to filter out the events not relevant to<br>your client in your client code. For most applications, one<br>is only interested in messages, so one specifies:<br>`"event_types": ["message"]`<br><br>Event types not supported by the server are ignored, in order to simplify<br>the implementation of client apps that support multiple server versions.<br>|
|» narrow|body|[Narrow](#schemanarrow)|false|A JSON-encoded array of arrays of length 2 indicating the<br>[narrow filter(s)](/api/construct-narrow) for which you'd<br>like to receive events for.<br><br>For example, to receive events for direct messages (including<br>group direct messages) received by the user, one can use<br>`"narrow": [["is", "dm"]]`.<br><br>Unlike the API for [fetching messages](/api/get-messages),<br>this narrow parameter is simply a filter on messages that the<br>user receives through their channel subscriptions (or because<br>they are a recipient of a direct message).<br><br>This means that a client that requests a `narrow` filter of<br>`[["channel", "Denmark"]]` will receive events for new messages<br>sent to that channel while the user is subscribed to that<br>channel. The client will not receive any message events at all<br>if the user is not subscribed to `"Denmark"`.<br><br>Newly created bot users are not usually subscribed to any<br>channels, so bots using this API need to be<br>[subscribed](/api/subscribe) to any channels whose messages<br>you'd like them to process using this endpoint.<br><br>See the `all_public_streams` parameter for how to process all<br>public channel messages in an organization.<br><br>**Changes**: See [changes section](/api/construct-narrow#changes)<br>of search/narrow filter documentation.<br>|
|» all_public_streams|body|[AllPublicChannels](#schemaallpublicchannels)|false|Whether you would like to request message events from all public<br>channels. Useful for workflow bots that you'd like to see all new messages<br>sent to public channels. (You can also subscribe the user to private channels).<br>|

<h3 id="postreal-time-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Get topics in a channel

<a id="opIdget-stream-topics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/users/me/1/topics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/me/{stream_id}/topics`

Get all topics the user has access to in a specific channel.

Note that for [private channels with
protected history](/help/channel-permissions#private-channels),
the user will only have access to topics of messages sent after they
[subscribed to](/api/subscribe) the channel. Similarly, a user's
[bot](/help/bots-overview#bot-type) will only have access to messages
sent after the bot was subscribed to the channel, instead of when the
user subscribed.

**Changes**: Before Zulip 12.0 (feature level 480), this
endpoint was not supported for archived channels.

Previously,<br>the empty string was not a valid topic.<br>|

```json
    },

      "max_id": 23,
      "name": "Denmark1"
    },

      "name": "Denmark2"
    }
```

## Get subscribed channels

<a id="opIdget-subscriptions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/users/me/subscriptions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/me/subscriptions`

Get all channels that the user is subscribed to.


<h3 id="get-subscribed-channels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|include_subscribers|query|string|false|Whether each returned channel object should include a `subscribers`<br>field containing a list of the user IDs of its subscribers.<br><br>Client apps supporting organizations with many thousands of users<br>should not pass `true`, because the full subscriber matrix may be<br>several megabytes of data. The `partial` value, combined with the<br>`subscriber_count` and fetching subscribers for individual channels as<br>needed, is recommended to support client app features where<br>channel subscriber data is useful.<br><br>If a client passes `partial` for this parameter, the server may,<br>for some channels, return a subset of the channel's subscribers<br>in the `partial_subscribers` field instead of the `subscribers` field,<br>which always contains the complete set of subscribers.<br><br>The server guarantees that it will always return a `subscribers`<br>field for channels with fewer than 250 total subscribers. When<br>returning a `partial_subscribers` field, the server guarantees<br>that all bot users and users active within the last 14 days will<br>be included. For other cases, the server may use its discretion<br>to determine which channels and users to include, balancing between<br>payload size and usefulness of the data provided to the client.<br><br>**Changes**: The `partial` value is new in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 412).<br><br>New in Zulip 2.1.0.<br>|

## Subscribe to a channel

<a id="opIdsubscribe"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/users/me/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'subscriptions=%5B%7B%22name%22%3A%22Verona%22%2C%22description%22%3A%22Italian%20city%22%7D%5D&principals=%5B11%5D&authorization_errors_fatal=false&announce=true&invite_only=true&is_web_public=true&is_default_stream=true&history_public_to_subscribers=false&message_retention_days=20&default_push_notifications=true&topics_policy=inherit&can_add_subscribers_group=%7B%7D&can_remove_subscribers_group=%7B%7D&can_administer_channel_group=%7B%7D&can_delete_any_message_group=%7B%7D&can_delete_own_message_group=%7B%7D&can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group=%7B%7D&can_move_messages_within_channel_group=%7B%7D&can_send_message_group=%7B%7D&can_subscribe_group=%7B%7D&can_resolve_topics_group=%7B%7D&can_create_topic_group=%7B%7D&folder_id=1&send_new_subscription_messages=true'
```

`POST /users/me/subscriptions`

Subscribe one or more users to one or more channels.

If any of the specified channels do not exist, they are automatically
created. The initial [channel settings](/api/update-stream) will be determined
by the optional parameters, like `invite_only`, detailed below.

Note that the ability to subscribe oneself and/or other users
to a specified channel depends on the [channel's permissions
settings](/help/channel-permissions).

**Changes**: Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 362),
subscriptions in archived channels could not be modified.

Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 357), the
`can_subscribe_group` permission, which allows members of the
group to subscribe themselves to the channel, did not exist.

Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 349), a user cannot subscribe
other users to a private channel without being subscribed
to that channel themselves. Now, If a user is part of
`can_add_subscribers_group`, they can subscribe themselves or other
users to a private channel without being subscribed to that channel.

Removed `stream_post_policy` and `is_announcement_only`
parameters in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 333), as permission to post
in the channel is now controlled by `can_send_message_group`.

Before Zulip 8.0 (feature level 208), if a user specified by the
[`principals`][principals-param] parameter was a deactivated user,
or did not exist, then an HTTP status code of 403 was returned with
`code: "UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL"` in the error response. As of this
feature level, an HTTP status code of 400 is returned with
`code: "BAD_REQUEST"` in the error response for these cases.

[principals-param]: /api/subscribe#parameter-principals


> Body parameter

```yaml
subscriptions:
  -
    name: Verona
    description: Italian city
principals:
  - 11
authorization_errors_fatal: false
announce: true
invite_only: true
is_web_public: true
is_default_stream: true
history_public_to_subscribers: false
message_retention_days: "20"
default_push_notifications: true
topics_policy: inherit
can_add_subscribers_group: {}
can_remove_subscribers_group: {}
can_administer_channel_group: {}
can_delete_any_message_group: {}
can_delete_own_message_group: {}
can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group: {}
can_move_messages_within_channel_group: {}
can_send_message_group: {}
can_subscribe_group: {}
can_resolve_topics_group: {}
can_create_topic_group: {}
folder_id: 1
send_new_subscription_messages: true
```

<h3 id="subscribe-to-a-channel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» subscriptions|body|[object]|true|An array of objects containing information about the<br>channels that users will be subscribed to.<br><br>For each channel, there must be a key `name` and value<br>specifying the name of the channel. If a channel with that<br>name does not exist, then a new channel is created.<br>|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the channel.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_stream_name_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum channel name length.<br>|
|» » description|body|string|false|The [description](/help/change-the-channel-description)<br>to use for a new channel being created, in text/markdown format.<br><br>See the help center article on [message<br>formatting](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown)<br>for details on Zulip-flavored Markdown.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_stream_description_length` returned<br>by the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to<br>determine the maximum channel description length.<br>|
|» » color|body|string|false|The hex value of the user's display color for the channel.<br>The server will return an error if the value is not a valid<br>hex color code.<br><br>This color is only applied to subscriptions that are newly<br>created by this request. Users who are already subscribed to<br>the channel, or who were subscribed to it in the past, keep<br>their existing display color. If this key is omitted, the<br>server assigns each new subscriber a display color, preferring<br>one that they are not already using for another channel.<br><br>Some clients compute a placeholder color when displaying the<br>current user's unsubscribed channels so that they don't all<br>show up in a list with the same color. If a client does this,<br>then it should pass the placeholder color here so that the<br>channel's color doesn't change when the current user is<br>subscribed.<br>|
|» principals|body|[Principals](#schemaprincipals)|false|A list of user IDs (preferred) or Zulip API email<br>addresses of the users to be subscribed to or unsubscribed<br>from the channels specified in the `subscriptions` parameter.<br><br>If not provided, then the requesting user/bot will be<br>subscribed/unsubscribed from the specified channels.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 3.0 (feature level 9), only the<br>Zulip API email address string format was supported.<br>|
|» authorization_errors_fatal|body|boolean|false|A boolean specifying whether authorization errors (such as when the<br>requesting user is not authorized to access a private channel) should be<br>considered fatal or not. When `true`, an authorization error is reported<br>as such. When set to `false`, the response will be a 200 and any channels<br>where the request encountered an authorization error will be listed<br>in the `unauthorized` key.<br>|
|» announce|body|boolean|false|If one of the channels specified did not exist previously and is thus created<br>by this call, this determines whether [notification bot](/help/configure-automated-notices)<br>will send an announcement about the new channel's creation.<br>|
|» invite_only|body|boolean|false|As described above, this endpoint will create a new channel if passed<br>a channel name that doesn't already exist. This parameters and the ones<br>that follow are used to request an initial configuration of a created<br>channel; they are ignored for channels that already exist.<br><br>This parameter determines whether any newly created channels will be<br>private channels.<br>|
|» is_web_public|body|boolean|false|This parameter determines whether any newly created channels will be<br>web-public channels.<br><br>Note that creating web-public channels requires the<br>`WEB_PUBLIC_STREAMS_ENABLED` [server setting][server-settings]<br>to be enabled on the Zulip server in question, the organization<br>to have enabled the `enable_spectator_access` realm setting, and<br>the current use to have permission under the organization's<br>`can_create_web_public_channel_group` realm setting.<br><br>[server-settings]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/production/settings.html<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 5.0 (feature level 98).<br>|
|» is_default_stream|body|boolean|false|This parameter determines whether any newly created channels will be<br>added as [default channels][default-channels] for new users joining<br>the organization.<br><br>[default-channels]: /help/set-default-channels-for-new-users<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 200). Previously, default channel status<br>could only be changed using the [dedicated API endpoint](/api/add-default-stream).<br>|
|» history_public_to_subscribers|body|[HistoryPublicToSubscribers](#schemahistorypublictosubscribers)|false|Whether the channel's message history should be available to<br>newly subscribed members, or users can only access messages<br>they actually received while subscribed to the channel.<br><br>Corresponds to the shared history option for<br>[private channels](/help/channel-permissions#private-channels).<br>|
|» message_retention_days|body|[MessageRetentionDays](#schemamessageretentiondays)|false|Number of days that messages sent to this channel will be stored<br>before being automatically deleted by the [message retention<br>policy](/help/message-retention-policy). Two special string format<br>values are supported:<br><br>- `"realm_default"`: Return to the organization-level setting.<br>- `"unlimited"`: Retain messages forever.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 5.0 (feature level 91), retaining<br>messages forever was encoded using `"forever"` instead of<br>`"unlimited"`.<br><br>New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 17).<br>|
|» default_push_notifications|body|[DefaultPushNotifications](#schemadefaultpushnotifications)|false|Whether mobile push notifications will be enabled by default when a<br>user first subscribes to this channel, potentially overriding the<br>user's [default mobile notification<br>setting](/help/channel-notifications#configure-default-notifications-for-all-channels)<br>for channel messages.<br><br>Because this default is applied only the first time a user<br>subscribes, unsubscribing and resubscribing a user does not reset<br>their preference to this channel default.<br><br>Only organization administrators can set or modify this value.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 507).<br>|
|» topics_policy|body|[TopicsPolicy](#schematopicspolicy)|false|Whether [named topics](/help/introduction-to-topics) and the empty<br>topic (i.e., ["general chat" topic](/help/general-chat-topic))<br>are enabled in this channel.<br><br>- `"inherit"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this channel,<br>  and the [organization-level `realm_topics_policy`][realm-topics-policy]<br>  is used for whether messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel.<br>- `"allow_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to both named topics and<br>  the empty topic in this channel.<br>- `"disable_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this<br>  channel, but the empty topic is disabled.<br>- `"empty_topic_only"`: Messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel, but named topics are disabled. See ["general chat"<br>  channels](/help/general-chat-channels).<br><br>The `"empty_topic_only"` policy can only be set if all existing messages<br>in the channel are already in the empty topic.<br><br>When creating a new channel, if the `topics_policy` is not specified, the<br>`"inherit"` option will be set.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 11.0 (feature level 404), the `"empty_topic_only"`<br>option was added.<br><br>New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 392).<br><br>[realm-topics-policy]: /help/require-topics#set-the-default-general-chat-topic-configuration<br>|
|» can_add_subscribers_group|body|[ChannelCanAddSubscribersGroup](#schemachannelcanaddsubscribersgroup)|false|none|
|» can_remove_subscribers_group|body|[CanRemoveSubscribersGroup](#schemacanremovesubscribersgroup)|false|none|
|» can_administer_channel_group|body|[CanAdministerChannelGroup](#schemacanadministerchannelgroup)|false|none|
|» can_delete_any_message_group|body|[CanDeleteAnyMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteanymessagegroup)|false|none|
|» can_delete_own_message_group|body|[CanDeleteOwnMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteownmessagegroup)|false|none|
|» can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group|body|[CanMoveMessagesOutOfChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessagesoutofchannelgroup)|false|none|
|» can_move_messages_within_channel_group|body|[CanMoveMessagesWithinChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessageswithinchannelgroup)|false|none|
|» can_send_message_group|body|[CanSendMessageGroup](#schemacansendmessagegroup)|false|none|
|» can_subscribe_group|body|[CanSubscribeGroup](#schemacansubscribegroup)|false|none|
|» can_resolve_topics_group|body|[CanResolveTopicsGroup](#schemacanresolvetopicsgroup)|false|none|
|» can_create_topic_group|body|[CanCreateTopicGroup](#schemacancreatetopicgroup)|false|none|
|» folder_id|body|integer|false|This parameter adds the newly created channel to the specified<br>[channel folder](/help/channel-folders).<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 389).<br>|
|» send_new_subscription_messages|body|[SendNewSubscriptionMessages](#schemasendnewsubscriptionmessages)|false|Whether any other users newly subscribed via this request should be<br>sent a direct message, from Notification Bot, notifying them about their<br>new subscription.<br><br>No direct messages are sent for any channels that are created as part of<br>this request, regardless of the value of this parameter.<br><br>The server will never send direct messages when the total number of users<br>who were subscribed to channels in this request was more than the value<br>of `max_bulk_subscription_messages`, which is available in the [`POST<br>/register`](/api/register-queue) response.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 11.0 (feature level 397), new subscribers<br>were always sent a Notification Bot direct message, which was unduly<br>expensive when bulk-subscribing thousands of users to a channel.<br>|

## Unsubscribe from a channel

<a id="opIdunsubscribe"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/users/me/subscriptions \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'subscriptions=%5B%22Verona%22%2C%22Denmark%22%5D&principals=%5B11%5D&send_messages_to_removed_subscribers=true'
```

`DELETE /users/me/subscriptions`

Unsubscribe yourself or other users from one or more channels.

In addition to managing the current user's subscriptions, this
endpoint can be used to remove other users from channels. This
is possible in 3 situations:

- Organization administrators can remove any user from any
  channel.
- Users can remove a bot that they own from any channel that
  the user [can access](/help/channel-permissions).
- Users can unsubscribe any user from a channel if they [have
  access](/help/channel-permissions) to the channel and are a
  member of the [user group](/api/get-user-groups) specified
  by the [`can_remove_subscribers_group`][can-remove-parameter]
  for the channel.

When other users are removed from a channel, they may receive
a direct message notifying them that they were unsubscribed by
the current user; see
[`send_messages_to_removed_subscribers`][send-notifications-param]
below.

**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 13.0 (feature level 515), the
server never sent direct messages to users who were unsubscribed
from one or more channels by the current user.

Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 362), subscriptions in archived
channels could not be modified.

Before Zulip 8.0 (feature level 208), if a user specified by
the [`principals`][principals-param] parameter was a
deactivated user, or did not exist, then an HTTP status code
of 403 was returned with `code: "UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL"` in
the error response. As of this feature level, an HTTP status
code of 400 is returned with `code: "BAD_REQUEST"` in the
error response for these cases.

Before Zulip 8.0 (feature level 197),
the `can_remove_subscribers_group` setting
was named `can_remove_subscribers_group_id`.

Before Zulip 7.0 (feature level 161), the
`can_remove_subscribers_group_id` for all channels was always
the system group for organization administrators.

Before Zulip 6.0 (feature level 145), users had no special
privileges for managing bots that they own.

[principals-param]: /api/unsubscribe#parameter-principals
[can-remove-parameter]: /api/subscribe#parameter-can_remove_subscribers_group
[send-notifications-param]: /api/unsubscribe#parameter-send_messages_to_removed_subscribers


> Body parameter

```yaml
subscriptions:
  - Verona
  - Denmark
principals:
  - 11
send_messages_to_removed_subscribers: true
```

<h3 id="unsubscribe-from-a-channel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» subscriptions|body|[string]|true|A list of channel names to unsubscribe from. This parameter is called<br>`streams` in our Python API.<br>|
|» principals|body|[Principals](#schemaprincipals)|false|A list of user IDs (preferred) or Zulip API email<br>addresses of the users to be subscribed to or unsubscribed<br>from the channels specified in the `subscriptions` parameter.<br><br>If not provided, then the requesting user/bot will be<br>subscribed/unsubscribed from the specified channels.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 3.0 (feature level 9), only the<br>Zulip API email address string format was supported.<br>|
|» send_messages_to_removed_subscribers|body|boolean|false|Whether other users unsubscribed via this request should be sent a<br>direct message, from Notification Bot, notifying them that they<br>were unsubscribed and by whom.<br><br>The server will never send direct messages when the total number of<br>users who were unsubscribed from channels in this request was more<br>than the value of `max_bulk_subscription_messages`, which is<br>available in the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) response.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 515).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "messages_sent_to_removed_subscribers": true,
  "not_removed": [],
  "removed": [
    "testing-help"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Channel 'nonexistent' does not exist",
  "code": "STREAM_DOES_NOT_EXIST",
  "stream": "nonexistent"
}
```

<h3 id="unsubscribe-from-a-channel-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

<h3 id="unsubscribe-from-a-channel-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|result|string|true|none|none|

Clients may<br>find this value useful to communicate with users about the<br>effect of this request.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 515).<br>|

## Topic muting

<a id="opIdmute-topic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/users/me/subscriptions/muted_topics \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'stream_id=43&stream=Denmark&topic=dinner&op=add'
```

`PATCH /users/me/subscriptions/muted_topics`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

[Mute or unmute a topic](/help/mute-a-topic) within a channel that
the current user is subscribed to.

**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 7.0 (feature level 170). Clients connecting
to newer servers should use the [POST /user_topics](/api/update-user-topic)
endpoint, as this endpoint may be removed in a future release.

Before Zulip 7.0 (feature level 169), this endpoint
returned an error if asked to mute a topic that was already muted
or asked to unmute a topic that had not previously been muted.


> Body parameter

```yaml
stream_id: 43
stream: Denmark
topic: dinner
op: add
```

<h3 id="topic-muting-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» stream_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the channel to access.<br><br>Clients must provide either `stream` or `stream_id` as a parameter<br>to this endpoint, but not both.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 2.0.0.<br>|
|» stream|body|string|false|The name of the channel to access.<br><br>Clients must provide either `stream` or `stream_id` as a parameter<br>to this endpoint, but not both. Clients should use `stream_id`<br>instead of the `stream` parameter when possible.<br>|
|» topic|body|string|true|The topic to (un)mute. Note that the request will succeed regardless of<br>whether any messages have been sent to the specified topic.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_topic_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum topic length.<br>|
|» op|body|string|true|Whether to mute (`add`) or unmute (`remove`) the provided topic.<br>|

|» op|add|
|» op|remove|

## Update personal preferences for a topic

<a id="opIdupdate-user-topic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/user_topics \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'stream_id=1&topic=dinner&visibility_policy=1'
```

`POST /user_topics`

This endpoint is used to update the personal preferences for a topic,
such as the topic's visibility policy, which is used to implement
[mute a topic](/help/mute-a-topic) and related features.

This endpoint can be used to update the visibility policy for the single
channel and topic pair indicated by the parameters for a user.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 7.0 (feature level 170). Previously,
toggling whether a topic was muted or unmuted was managed by the
[PATCH /users/me/subscriptions/muted_topics](/api/mute-topic) endpoint.


> Body parameter

```yaml
stream_id: 1
topic: dinner
visibility_policy: 1
```

<h3 id="update-personal-preferences-for-a-topic-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» stream_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the channel to access.<br>|
|» topic|body|string|true|The topic for which the personal preferences needs to be updated.<br>Note that the request will succeed regardless of whether<br>any messages have been sent to the specified topic.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_topic_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum topic length.<br><br>Note: When the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name` found in<br>the [POST /register](/api/register-queue) response is used for this<br>parameter, it is interpreted as an empty string.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334), empty string<br>was not a valid topic name for channel messages.<br>|
|» visibility_policy|body|integer|true|Controls which visibility policy to set.<br><br>- 0 = None. Removes the visibility policy previously set for the topic.<br>- 1 = Muted. [Mutes the topic](/help/mute-a-topic) in a channel.<br>- 2 = Unmuted. [Unmutes the topic](/help/mute-a-topic) in a muted channel.<br>- 3 = Followed. [Follows the topic](/help/follow-a-topic).<br><br>In an unmuted channel, a topic visibility policy of unmuted will have the<br>same effect as the "None" visibility policy.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 7.0 (feature level 219), added followed as<br>a visibility policy option.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» visibility_policy|0|
|» visibility_policy|1|
|» visibility_policy|2|
|» visibility_policy|3|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

|200|OK|Success.|[JsonSuccess](#schemajsonsuccess)|

## Get a user's subscribed channels

<a id="opIdget-user-channels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/users/12/channels \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /users/{user_id}/channels`

Gets the list of channels that the target user is subscribed to.

The [channel security model](/help/channel-permissions) means only those
subscribed channels to which the acting user has metadata access are
returned.

For organization administrators, this is guaranteed to be all channels
the target user is subscribed to, since organization administrators
implicitly have metadata access to all channels.

**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 12.0 (feature level 458), target users that
were bots resulted in a permissions error.

New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 440).


<h3 id="get-a-users-subscribed-channels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|integer|true|The target user's ID.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "subscribed_channel_ids": [
    3,
    5,
    10
  ]
}
```

## Bulk update subscription settings

<a id="opIdupdate-subscription-settings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/users/me/subscriptions/properties \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'subscription_data=%5B%7B%22stream_id%22%3A1%2C%22property%22%3A%22pin_to_top%22%2C%22value%22%3Atrue%7D%2C%7B%22stream_id%22%3A3%2C%22property%22%3A%22color%22%2C%22value%22%3A%22%23f00f00%22%7D%5D'
```

`POST /users/me/subscriptions/properties`

Update the current user's personal settings for channels they are
subscribed to. These settings include [color](/help/change-the-color-of-a-channel),
[muting](/help/mute-a-channel), [pinning](/help/pin-a-channel)
and [per-channel notification settings](/help/channel-notifications).

There is a single channel alternative to this bulk endpoint:
[`POST /users/me/subscriptions/{stream_id}`](/api/update-subscription-property).

**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 5.0 (feature level 111), the response object
included the `subscription_data` in the request. The endpoint now returns
the more ergonomic [`ignored_parameters_unsupported`][ignored-parameters]
array instead.

[ignored-parameters]: /api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters


> Body parameter

```yaml
subscription_data:
  -
    stream_id: 1
    property: pin_to_top
    value: true
  -
    stream_id: 3
    property: color
    value: "#f00f00"
```

<h3 id="bulk-update-subscription-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» subscription_data|body|[object]|true|A list of objects that describe the changes that should be applied in<br>each subscription. Each object represents a subscription, and must have<br>a `stream_id` key that identifies the channel, as well as the `property`<br>being modified and its new `value`.<br>|
|» » stream_id|body|integer|true|The unique ID of a channel.<br>|
|» » property|body|[SubscriptionProperty](#schemasubscriptionproperty)|true|One of the channel properties described below:<br><br>- `"color"`: The hex value of the user's display color for the channel.<br><br>- `"is_muted"`: Whether the channel is [muted](/help/mute-a-channel).<br><br>  **Changes**: As of Zulip 6.0 (feature level 139), updating either<br>  `"is_muted"` or `"in_home_view"` generates two [subscription update<br>  events](/api/get-events#subscription-update), one for each property,<br>  that are sent to clients. Prior to this feature level, updating either<br>  property only generated a subscription update event for<br>  `"in_home_view"`. <br><br>  Prior to Zulip 2.1.0, this feature was represented<br>  by the more confusingly named `"in_home_view"` (with the<br>  opposite value: `in_home_view=!is_muted`); for<br>  backwards-compatibility, modern Zulip still accepts that property.<br><br>- `"pin_to_top"`: Whether to pin the channel at the top of the channel list.<br><br>- `"desktop_notifications"`: Whether to show desktop notifications<br>  for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"audible_notifications"`: Whether to play a sound<br>  notification for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"push_notifications"`: Whether to trigger a mobile push<br>  notification for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"email_notifications"`: Whether to trigger an email<br>  notification for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"wildcard_mentions_notify"`: Whether wildcard mentions trigger<br>  notifications as though they were personal mentions in this channel.<br>|
|» » value|body|[SubscriptionPropertyValue](#schemasubscriptionpropertyvalue)|true|The new value of the property being modified.<br><br>If the property is `"color"`, then `value` is a string<br>representing the hex value of the user's display<br>color for the channel. For all other above properties,<br>`value` is a boolean.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » property|color|
|» » property|is_muted|
|» » property|in_home_view|
|» » property|pin_to_top|
|» » property|desktop_notifications|
|» » property|audible_notifications|
|» » property|push_notifications|
|» » property|email_notifications|
|» » property|wildcard_mentions_notify|

```json
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|

Prior to this feature level, updating either<br>  property only generated a subscription update event for<br>  `"in_home_view"`. <br><br>  Prior to Zulip 2.1.0, this feature was represented<br>  by the more confusingly named `"in_home_view"` (with the<br>  opposite value: `in_home_view=!is_muted`); for<br>  backwards-compatibility, modern Zulip still accepts that property.<br><br>- `"pin_to_top"`: Whether to pin the channel at the top of the channel list.<br><br>- `"desktop_notifications"`: Whether to show desktop notifications<br>  for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"audible_notifications"`: Whether to play a sound<br>  notification for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"push_notifications"`: Whether to trigger a mobile push<br>  notification for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"email_notifications"`: Whether to trigger an email<br>  notification for all messages sent to the channel.<br><br>- `"wildcard_mentions_notify"`: Whether wildcard mentions trigger<br>  notifications as though they were personal mentions in this channel.<br>|
|» value|body|[SubscriptionPropertyValue](#schemasubscriptionpropertyvalue)|true|The new value of the property being modified.<br><br>If the property is `"color"`, then `value` is a string<br>representing the hex value of the user's display<br>color for the channel. For all other above properties,<br>`value` is a boolean.<br>|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /streams`

Get all channels that the user [has access to](/help/channel-permissions).


<h3 id="get-all-channels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|include_public|query|boolean|false|Include all public channels.<br>|
|include_web_public|query|boolean|false|Include all web-public channels.<br>|
|include_subscribed|query|boolean|false|Include all channels that the user is subscribed to.<br>|

|include_all_active|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated parameter to include all channels. The user must<br>have administrative privileges to use this parameter.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 10.0 (feature level<br>356). Clients interacting with newer servers should use<br>the equivalent `include_all` parameter, which does not<br>incorrectly hint that this parameter, and not<br>`exclude_archived`, controls whether archived channels<br>appear in the response.<br>|
|include_all|query|boolean|false|Include all channels that the user has metadata access to.<br><br>For organization administrators, this will be all channels<br>in the organization, since organization administrators<br>implicitly have metadata access to all channels.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 356). On older<br>versions, use `include_all_active`, which this replaces.<br>|
|include_default|query|boolean|false|Include all default channels for the user's realm.<br>|
|include_owner_subscribed|query|boolean|false|If the user is a bot, include all channels that the bot's owner is<br>subscribed to.<br>|
|include_can_access_content|query|boolean|false|Include all the channels that the user has content access to.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 356).<br>|
