See ["general chat"<br>  channels](/help/general-chat-channels).<br><br>The `"empty_topic_only"` policy can only be set if all existing messages<br>in the channel are already in the empty topic.<br><br>When creating a new channel, if the `topics_policy` is not specified, the<br>`"inherit"` option will be set.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 11.0 (feature level 404), the `"empty_topic_only"`<br>option was added.<br><br>New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 392).<br><br>[realm-topics-policy]: /help/require-topics#set-the-default-general-chat-topic-configuration<br>|
|» first_message_id|integer \| null|true|none|The ID of the first message in the channel.<br><br>Intended to help clients determine whether they need to display<br>UI like the "show all topics" widget that would suggest the channel<br>has older history that can be accessed.<br><br>Is `null` for channels with no message history.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 2.1.0.<br>|

Previously, clients implemented the<br>demote_inactive_streams from local message history, resulting in a choppy loading<br>experience.<br>|

## Get a channel by ID

<a id="opIdget-stream-by-id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/streams/1 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /streams/{stream_id}`

Fetch details for the channel with the ID `stream_id`.

**Changes**: Before Zulip 12.0 (feature level 480), this
endpoint was not supported for archived channels.

New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 132).


<h3 id="get-a-channel-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the channel to access.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "stream": {
    "description": "A Scandinavian country",
    "first_message_id": 1,
    "folder_id": 1,
    "is_recently_active": true,
    "history_public_to_subscribers": true,
    "date_created": 1691057093,
    "creator_id": null,
    "invite_only": false,
    "is_announcement_only": false,
    "is_archived": false,
    "is_web_public": false,
    "message_retention_days": null,
    "default_push_notifications": false,
    "name": "Denmark",
    "rendered_description": "<p>A Scandinavian country</p>",
    "stream_id": 7,
    "stream_post_policy": 1,
    "can_add_subscribers_group": 2,
    "can_remove_subscribers_group": 2,
    "can_subscribe_group": 2,
    "stream_weekly_traffic": null,
    "subscriber_count": 12
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Invalid channel ID",
  "code": "BAD_REQUEST"
}
```

## Update a channel

<a id="opIdupdate-stream"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/streams/1 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'description=Discuss%20Italian%20history%20and%20travel%20destinations.&new_name=Italy&is_private=true&is_web_public=true&history_public_to_subscribers=false&is_default_stream=false&message_retention_days=20&default_push_notifications=true&is_archived=true&folder_id=1&topics_policy=inherit&can_add_subscribers_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_remove_subscribers_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_administer_channel_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_delete_any_message_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_delete_own_message_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_move_messages_within_channel_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_send_message_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_subscribe_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_resolve_topics_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&can_create_topic_group=%7B%22new%22%3A%7B%7D%2C%22old%22%3A%7B%7D%7D'
```

`PATCH /streams/{stream_id}`

Configure the channel with the ID `stream_id`. This endpoint supports
an organization administrator editing any property of a channel,
including:

- Channel [name](/help/rename-a-channel) and [description](/help/change-the-channel-description)
- Channel [permissions](/help/channel-permissions), including
  [privacy](/help/change-the-privacy-of-a-channel) and [who can
  send](/help/channel-posting-policy).

Note that an organization administrator's ability to change a
[private channel's permissions](/help/channel-permissions#private-channels)
depends on them being subscribed to the channel.

**Changes**: Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 362), channel privacy could not be
edited for archived channels.

Removed `stream_post_policy` and `is_announcement_only`
parameters in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 333), as permission to post
in the channel is now controlled by `can_send_message_group`.


> Body parameter

```yaml
description: Discuss Italian history and travel destinations.
new_name: Italy
is_private: true
is_web_public: true
history_public_to_subscribers: false
is_default_stream: false
message_retention_days: "20"
default_push_notifications: true
is_archived: true
folder_id: 1
topics_policy: inherit
can_add_subscribers_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_remove_subscribers_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_administer_channel_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_delete_any_message_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_delete_own_message_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_move_messages_within_channel_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_send_message_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_subscribe_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_resolve_topics_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
can_create_topic_group:
  new: {}
  old: {}
```

<h3 id="update-a-channel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the channel to access.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The new [description](/help/change-the-channel-description) for<br>the channel, in [Zulip-flavored Markdown](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown) format.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_stream_description_length` returned<br>by the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to<br>determine the maximum channel description length.<br><br>**Changes**: Removed unnecessary JSON-encoding of this parameter in<br>Zulip 4.0 (feature level 64).<br>|
|» new_name|body|string|false|The new name for the channel.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_stream_name_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum channel name length.<br><br>**Changes**: Removed unnecessary JSON-encoding of this parameter in<br>Zulip 4.0 (feature level 64).<br>|
|» is_private|body|boolean|false|Change whether the channel is a private channel.<br>|
|» is_web_public|body|boolean|false|Change whether the channel is a web-public channel.<br><br>Note that creating web-public channels requires the<br>`WEB_PUBLIC_STREAMS_ENABLED` [server setting][server-settings]<br>to be enabled on the Zulip server in question, the organization<br>to have enabled the `enable_spectator_access` realm setting, and<br>the current use to have permission under the organization's<br>`can_create_web_public_channel_group` realm setting.<br><br>[server-settings]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/production/settings.html<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 5.0 (feature level 98).<br>|
|» history_public_to_subscribers|body|boolean|false|Whether the channel's message history should be available to<br>newly subscribed members, or users can only access messages<br>they actually received while subscribed to the channel.<br><br>Corresponds to the shared history option for<br>[private channels](/help/channel-permissions#private-channels).<br><br>It's an error for this parameter to be false for a public or<br>web-public channel and when is_private is false.<br><br>This can only be `false` if `can_create_topic_group` for the channel<br>is the `role:everyone` [system group][system-groups].<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 6.0 (feature level 136), `history_public_to_subscribers`<br>was silently ignored unless the request also contained either `is_private` or<br>`is_web_public`.<br><br>[system-groups]: /api/group-setting-values#system-groups<br>|
|» is_default_stream|body|boolean|false|Add or remove the channel as a [default channel][default-channel]<br>for new users joining the organization.<br><br>[default-channel]: /help/set-default-channels-for-new-users<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 200). Previously, default channel status<br>could only be changed using the [dedicated API endpoint](/api/add-default-stream).<br>|
|» message_retention_days|body|[MessageRetentionDays](#schemamessageretentiondays)|false|Number of days that messages sent to this channel will be stored<br>before being automatically deleted by the [message retention<br>policy](/help/message-retention-policy). Two special string format<br>values are supported:<br><br>- `"realm_default"`: Return to the organization-level setting.<br>- `"unlimited"`: Retain messages forever.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 5.0 (feature level 91), retaining<br>messages forever was encoded using `"forever"` instead of<br>`"unlimited"`.<br><br>New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 17).<br>|
|» default_push_notifications|body|[DefaultPushNotifications](#schemadefaultpushnotifications)|false|Whether mobile push notifications will be enabled by default when a<br>user first subscribes to this channel, potentially overriding the<br>user's [default mobile notification<br>setting](/help/channel-notifications#configure-default-notifications-for-all-channels)<br>for channel messages.<br><br>Because this default is applied only the first time a user<br>subscribes, unsubscribing and resubscribing a user does not reset<br>their preference to this channel default.<br><br>Only organization administrators can set or modify this value.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 507).<br>|
|» is_archived|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether the channel is<br>[archived](/help/archive-a-channel) or<br>unarchived. Currently only allows unarchiving<br>previously archived channels.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 388).<br>|
|» folder_id|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the new [channel folder](/help/channel-folders) to which the<br>channel should belong.<br><br>A `null` value indicates the user wants to remove the channel from its<br>current channel folder.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 389).<br>|
|» topics_policy|body|[TopicsPolicy](#schematopicspolicy)|false|Whether [named topics](/help/introduction-to-topics) and the empty<br>topic (i.e., ["general chat" topic](/help/general-chat-topic))<br>are enabled in this channel.<br><br>- `"inherit"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this channel,<br>  and the [organization-level `realm_topics_policy`][realm-topics-policy]<br>  is used for whether messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel.<br>- `"allow_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to both named topics and<br>  the empty topic in this channel.<br>- `"disable_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this<br>  channel, but the empty topic is disabled.<br>- `"empty_topic_only"`: Messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel, but named topics are disabled. See ["general chat"<br>  channels](/help/general-chat-channels).<br><br>The `"empty_topic_only"` policy can only be set if all existing messages<br>in the channel are already in the empty topic.<br><br>When creating a new channel, if the `topics_policy` is not specified, the<br>`"inherit"` option will be set.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 11.0 (feature level 404), the `"empty_topic_only"`<br>option was added.<br><br>New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 392).<br><br>[realm-topics-policy]: /help/require-topics#set-the-default-general-chat-topic-configuration<br>|
|» can_add_subscribers_group|body|object|false|none|

## Get channel's email address

<a id="opIdget-stream-email-address"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/streams/1/email_address \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /streams/{stream_id}/email_address`

Get email address of a channel.

Note that only users with permission to post messages in the channel
can access the channel's email address.

**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 12.0 (feature level 448), users without
permission to post messages in the channel could access the channel's email
if they had metadata access.

New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 226).


<h3 id="get-channels-email-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the channel to access.<br>|
|sender_id|query|integer|false|The ID of a user or bot which should appear as the sender when messages<br>are sent to the channel using the returned channel email address.<br><br>`sender_id` can be:<br><br>- ID of the current user.<br>- ID of the Email gateway bot. (Default value)<br>- ID of a bot owned by the current user.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 335).<br><br>Previously, the sender was always Email gateway bot.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "email": "test.af64447e9e39374841063747ade8e6b0.show-sender@testserver"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Invalid channel ID",
  "code": "BAD_REQUEST"
}
```

## Delete a topic

<a id="opIddelete-topic"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/streams/1/delete_topic \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'topic_name=new%20coffee%20machine'
```

`POST /streams/{stream_id}/delete_topic`

Delete all messages in a topic.

Topics are a field on messages (not an independent data structure), so
deleting all the messages in the topic deletes the topic from Zulip.

Because this endpoint deletes messages in batches, it is possible for
the request to time out after only deleting some messages in the topic.
When this happens, the `complete` boolean field in the success response
will be `false`. Clients should repeat the request when handling such a
response. If all messages in the topic were deleted, then the success
response will return `"complete": true`.

**Changes**: Before Zulip 9.0 (feature level 256), the server never sent
[`stream` op: `update`](/api/get-events#stream-update) events with an
updated `first_message_id` for a channel when the oldest message that
had been sent to it changed.

Before Zulip 8.0 (feature level 211), if the server's
processing was interrupted by a timeout, but some messages in the topic
were deleted, then it would return `"result": "partially_completed"`,
along with a `code` field for an error string, in the success response
to indicate that there was a timeout and that the client should repeat
the request.

As of Zulip 6.0 (feature level 154), instead of returning an error
response when a request times out after successfully deleting some of
the messages in the topic, a success response is returned with
`"result": "partially_completed"` to indicate that some messages were
deleted.

Before Zulip 6.0 (feature level 147), this request did a single atomic
operation, which could time out for very large topics. As of this
feature level, messages are deleted in batches, starting with the newest
messages, so that progress is made even if the request times out and
returns an error.


> Body parameter

```yaml
topic_name: new coffee machine
```

<h3 id="delete-a-topic-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the channel to access.<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» topic_name|body|string|true|The name of the topic to delete.<br><br>Note: When the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name` found in<br>the [POST /register](/api/register-queue) response is used for this<br>parameter, it is interpreted as an empty string.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334), empty string<br>was not a valid topic name for channel messages.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "complete": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Must be an organization administrator",
  "code": "UNAUTHORIZED_PRINCIPAL"
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-topic-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|msg|string|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|[IgnoredParametersUnsupported](#schemaignoredparametersunsupported)|false|none|An array of any parameters sent in the request that are not<br>supported by the endpoint.<br><br>See [error handling](/api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters) documentation<br>for details on this and its change history.<br>|
|result|object|true|none|none|

## Create a channel

<a id="opIdcreate-channel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/channels/create \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'name=music&description=Channel%20for%20discussing%20all%20things%20music!&subscribers=%5B17%2C12%5D&announce=true&invite_only=true&is_web_public=true&is_default_stream=true&folder_id=1&topics_policy=inherit&history_public_to_subscribers=false&message_retention_days=20&can_add_subscribers_group=%7B%7D&can_create_topic_group=%7B%7D&can_delete_any_message_group=%7B%7D&can_delete_own_message_group=%7B%7D&can_remove_subscribers_group=%7B%7D&can_administer_channel_group=%7B%7D&can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group=%7B%7D&can_move_messages_within_channel_group=%7B%7D&can_send_message_group=%7B%7D&can_subscribe_group=%7B%7D&can_resolve_topics_group=%7B%7D&default_push_notifications=true'
```

`POST /channels/create`

Create a new [channel](/help/create-channels), and optionally subscribe
users to the newly created channel.

The initial [channel settings](/api/update-stream) will be determined
by the optional parameters, like `invite_only`, detailed below.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 417). Previously, this was
only possible via the [`POST /api/subscribe`](/api/subscribe) endpoint,
which handles both channel subscription and creation.


> Body parameter

```yaml
name: music
description: "Channel for discussing all things music!"
subscribers:
  - 17
  - 12
announce: true
invite_only: true
is_web_public: true
is_default_stream: true
folder_id: 1
topics_policy: inherit
history_public_to_subscribers: false
message_retention_days: "20"
can_add_subscribers_group: {}
can_create_topic_group: {}
can_delete_any_message_group: {}
can_delete_own_message_group: {}
can_remove_subscribers_group: {}
can_administer_channel_group: {}
can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group: {}
can_move_messages_within_channel_group: {}
can_send_message_group: {}
can_subscribe_group: {}
can_resolve_topics_group: {}
default_push_notifications: true
```

<h3 id="create-a-channel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the new channel.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_stream_name_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum channel name length.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|The [description](/help/change-the-channel-description)<br>to use for the new channel being created, in text/markdown format.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_stream_description_length` returned<br>by the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to<br>determine the maximum channel description length.<br>|
|» subscribers|body|[integer]|true|A list of user IDs of the users to be subscribed to the new channel.<br>|
|» announce|body|boolean|false|This determines whether [notification bot](/help/configure-automated-notices)<br>will send an announcement about the new channel's creation.<br>|
|» invite_only|body|boolean|false|This parameter and the ones that follow are used to request an initial<br>configuration of the new channel.<br><br>This parameter determines whether the newly created channel will be<br>a [private channel](/help/channel-permissions#private-channels).<br>|
|» is_web_public|body|boolean|false|This parameter determines whether the newly created channel will be<br>a web-public channel.<br><br>Note that creating web-public channels requires the<br>`WEB_PUBLIC_STREAMS_ENABLED` [server setting][server-settings]<br>to be enabled on the Zulip server in question, the organization<br>to have enabled the `enable_spectator_access` realm setting, and<br>the current user to have permission under the organization's<br>`can_create_web_public_channel_group` realm setting.<br><br>[server-settings]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/stable/production/settings.html<br>|
|» is_default_stream|body|boolean|false|This parameter determines whether the newly created channel will be<br>added as a [default channel][default-channels] for new users joining<br>the organization.<br><br>[default-channels]: /help/set-default-channels-for-new-users<br>|
|» folder_id|body|integer|false|This parameter adds the newly created channel to the specified<br>[channel folder](/help/channel-folders).<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 389).<br>|
|» topics_policy|body|[TopicsPolicy](#schematopicspolicy)|false|Whether [named topics](/help/introduction-to-topics) and the empty<br>topic (i.e., ["general chat" topic](/help/general-chat-topic))<br>are enabled in this channel.<br><br>- `"inherit"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this channel,<br>  and the [organization-level `realm_topics_policy`][realm-topics-policy]<br>  is used for whether messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel.<br>- `"allow_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to both named topics and<br>  the empty topic in this channel.<br>- `"disable_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this<br>  channel, but the empty topic is disabled.<br>- `"empty_topic_only"`: Messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel, but named topics are disabled. See ["general chat"<br>  channels](/help/general-chat-channels).<br><br>The `"empty_topic_only"` policy can only be set if all existing messages<br>in the channel are already in the empty topic.<br><br>When creating a new channel, if the `topics_policy` is not specified, the<br>`"inherit"` option will be set.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 11.0 (feature level 404), the `"empty_topic_only"`<br>option was added.<br><br>New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 392).<br><br>[realm-topics-policy]: /help/require-topics#set-the-default-general-chat-topic-configuration<br>|
|» history_public_to_subscribers|body|[HistoryPublicToSubscribers](#schemahistorypublictosubscribers)|false|Whether the channel's message history should be available to<br>newly subscribed members, or users can only access messages<br>they actually received while subscribed to the channel.<br><br>Corresponds to the shared history option for<br>[private channels](/help/channel-permissions#private-channels).<br>|
|» message_retention_days|body|[MessageRetentionDays](#schemamessageretentiondays)|false|Number of days that messages sent to this channel will be stored<br>before being automatically deleted by the [message retention<br>policy](/help/message-retention-policy). Two special string format<br>values are supported:<br><br>- `"realm_default"`: Return to the organization-level setting.<br>- `"unlimited"`: Retain messages forever.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 5.0 (feature level 91), retaining<br>messages forever was encoded using `"forever"` instead of<br>`"unlimited"`.<br><br>New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 17).<br>|
|» can_add_subscribers_group|body|[ChannelCanAddSubscribersGroup](#schemachannelcanaddsubscribersgroup)|false|none|
|» can_create_topic_group|body|[CanCreateTopicGroup](#schemacancreatetopicgroup)|false|none|
|» can_delete_any_message_group|body|[CanDeleteAnyMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteanymessagegroup)|false|none|
|» can_delete_own_message_group|body|[CanDeleteOwnMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteownmessagegroup)|false|none|
|» can_remove_subscribers_group|body|[CanRemoveSubscribersGroup](#schemacanremovesubscribersgroup)|false|none|
|» can_administer_channel_group|body|[CanAdministerChannelGroup](#schemacanadministerchannelgroup)|false|none|
|» can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group|body|[CanMoveMessagesOutOfChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessagesoutofchannelgroup)|false|none|
|» can_move_messages_within_channel_group|body|[CanMoveMessagesWithinChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessageswithinchannelgroup)|false|none|
|» can_send_message_group|body|[CanSendMessageGroup](#schemacansendmessagegroup)|false|none|
|» can_subscribe_group|body|[CanSubscribeGroup](#schemacansubscribegroup)|false|none|
|» can_resolve_topics_group|body|[CanResolveTopicsGroup](#schemacanresolvetopicsgroup)|false|none|
|» default_push_notifications|body|[DefaultPushNotifications](#schemadefaultpushnotifications)|false|Whether mobile push notifications will be enabled by default when a<br>user first subscribes to this channel, potentially overriding the<br>user's [default mobile notification<br>setting](/help/channel-notifications#configure-default-notifications-for-all-channels)<br>for channel messages.<br><br>Because this default is applied only the first time a user<br>subscribes, unsubscribing and resubscribing a user does not reset<br>their preference to this channel default.<br><br>Only organization administrators can set or modify this value.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 507).<br>|

`GET /channel_folders`

## Reorder channel folders

<a id="opIdpatch-channel-folders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/channel_folders \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'order=%5B2%2C1%5D'
```

`PATCH /channel_folders`

Reorder the [channel folders](/help/channel-folders) in the user's
organization.

Channel folders are displayed in Zulip UI in order; this endpoint allows
administrative settings UI to change the ordering of channel folders.

This endpoint is used to implement the dragging feature described in the
[manage channel folders documentation](/help/manage-channel-folders).

**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 414).


> Body parameter

```yaml
order:
  - 2
  - 1
```

<h3 id="reorder-channel-folders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» order|body|[integer]|true|A list of channel folder IDs representing the new order.<br><br>This list must include the IDs of [all the organization's channel<br>folders](/api/get-channel-folders), including archived folders.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "result": "error",

  "code": "BAD_REQUEST"
}
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/channel_folders/1 \
```

`PATCH /channel_folders/{channel_folder_id}`

folder.

|» description|body|string|false|The new description of the channel folder.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_channel_folder_description_length`<br>returned by the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint<br>to determine the maximum channel folder description length.<br>|
|» is_archived|body|boolean|false|Whether to archive or unarchive the channel folder.<br>|

`GET /calls/bigbluebutton/create`

Create a video call URL for a BigBlueButton video call.
Requires [BigBlueButton 2.4+](/integrations/big-blue-button)
to be configured on the Zulip server.

user was given the moderator role on BigBlueButton calls, via

|voice_only|query|boolean|false|Configures whether the call is voice-only; if true,<br>disables cameras for all users. Only the call<br>creator/moderator can edit this configuration.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 337).<br>|

## Mark all messages as read

<a id="opIdmark-all-as-read"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/mark_all_as_read \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /mark_all_as_read`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Marks all of the current user's unread messages as read.

Because this endpoint marks messages as read in batches, it is possible
for the request to time out after only marking some messages as read.
When this happens, the `complete` boolean field in the success response
will be `false`. Clients should repeat the request when handling such a
response. If all messages were marked as read, then the success response
will return `"complete": true`.

**Changes**: Deprecated; clients should use the [update personal message
flags for narrow](/api/update-message-flags-for-narrow) endpoint instead
as this endpoint will be removed in a future release.

Before Zulip 8.0 (feature level 211), if the server's
processing was interrupted by a timeout, but some messages were marked
as read, then it would return `"result": "partially_completed"`, along
with a `code` field for an error string, in the success response to
indicate that there was a timeout and that the client should repeat the
request.

Before Zulip 6.0 (feature level 153), this request did a single atomic
operation, which could time out with 10,000s of unread messages to mark
as read. As of this feature level, messages are marked as read in
batches, starting with the newest messages, so that progress is made
even if the request times out. And, instead of returning an error when
the request times out and some messages have been marked as read, a
success response with `"result": "partially_completed"` is returned.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "complete": true
}
```

<h3 id="mark-all-messages-as-read-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|

<h3 id="mark-all-messages-as-read-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|msg|string|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|[IgnoredParametersUnsupported](#schemaignoredparametersunsupported)|false|none|An array of any parameters sent in the request that are not<br>supported by the endpoint.<br><br>See [error handling](/api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters) documentation<br>for details on this and its change history.<br>|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|msg|object|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|object|false|none|none|
|complete|boolean|true|none|Whether all unread messages were marked as read.<br><br>Will be `false` if the request successfully marked<br>some, but not all, messages as read.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|result|success|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Get messages

<a id="opIdget-messages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /messages`

This endpoint is the primary way to fetch messages. It is used by all official
Zulip clients (e.g. the web, desktop, mobile, and terminal clients) as well as
many bots, API clients, backup scripts, etc.

Most queries will specify a [narrow filter](/api/get-messages#parameter-narrow),
to fetch the messages matching any supported [search
query](/help/search-for-messages). If not specified, it will return messages
corresponding to the user's [combined feed](/help/combined-feed). There are two
ways to specify which messages matching the narrow filter to fetch:

- A range of messages, described by an `anchor` message ID (or a string-format
  specification of how the server should computer an anchor to use) and a maximum
  number of messages in each direction from that anchor.

- A rarely used variant (`message_ids`) where the client specifies the message IDs
  to fetch.

The server returns the matching messages, sorted by message ID, as well as some
metadata that makes it easy for a client to determine whether there are more
messages matching the query that were not returned due to the `num_before` and
`num_after` limits.

Note that a user's message history does not contain messages sent to
channels before they [subscribe](/api/subscribe), and newly created
bot users are not usually subscribed to any channels.

We recommend requesting at most 1000 messages in a batch, to avoid generating very
large HTTP responses. A maximum of 5000 messages can be obtained per request;
attempting to exceed this will result in an error.

**Changes**: The `message_ids` option is new in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 300).


<h3 id="get-messages-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|anchor|query|[Anchor](#schemaanchor)|false|Integer message ID to anchor fetching of new messages. Supports special<br>string values for when the client wants the server to compute the anchor<br>to use:<br><br>- `newest`: The most recent message.<br>- `oldest`: The oldest message.<br>- `first_unread`: The oldest unread message matching the<br>  query, if any; otherwise, the most recent message.<br>- `date`: The first message on or after the datetime indicated by the<br>  [`anchor_date`](#parameter-anchor_date), if any; otherwise, the most<br>  recent message.<br><br>**Changes**: The `date` value is new in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 445).<br><br>String values are new in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). The<br>`first_unread` functionality was supported in Zulip 2.1.x<br>and older by not sending `anchor` and using `use_first_unread_anchor`.<br><br>In Zulip 2.1.x and older, `oldest` can be emulated with<br>`"anchor": 0`, and `newest` with `"anchor": 10000000000000000`<br>(that specific large value works around a bug in Zulip<br>2.1.x and older in the `found_newest` return value).<br>|
|include_anchor|query|boolean|false|Whether a message with the specified ID matching the narrow<br>should be included.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 155).<br>|
|anchor_date|query|string|false|The date or datetime to use for finding the anchor message when `anchor` is<br>`date`. Accepted formats include ISO 8601 date-only strings<br>(e.g. `2005-04-18`) as well as full datetime strings<br>(e.g. `2005-04-18T12:34:56Z`). If only a date is provided, the datetime is set to<br>midnight (00:00) on that day in UTC. If no timezone is provided, UTC is<br>assumed.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 445).<br>|
|num_before|query|integer|false|The number of messages with IDs less than the anchor to retrieve.<br>Required if `message_ids` is not provided.<br>|
|num_after|query|integer|false|The number of messages with IDs greater than the anchor to retrieve.<br>Required if `message_ids` is not provided.<br>|
|narrow|query|[object \| [string]]|false|The narrow where you want to fetch the messages from. See how to<br>[construct a narrow](/api/construct-narrow).<br><br>Note that many narrows, including all that lack a `channel`, `channels`,<br>`stream`, or `streams` operator, search the user's personal message<br>history. See [searching shared<br>history](/help/search-for-messages#search-shared-history)<br>for details.<br><br>For example, if you would like to fetch messages from all public channels instead<br>of only the user's message history, then a specific narrow for<br>messages sent to all public channels can be used:<br>`{"operator": "channels", "operand": "public"}`.<br><br>Newly created bot users are not usually subscribed to any<br>channels, so bots using this API should either be<br>subscribed to appropriate channels or use a shared history<br>search narrow with this endpoint.<br><br>**Changes**: See [changes section](/api/construct-narrow#changes)<br>of search/narrow filter documentation.<br>|
|client_gravatar|query|boolean|false|Whether the client supports computing gravatars URLs. If<br>enabled, `avatar_url` will be included in the response only<br>if there is a Zulip avatar, and will be `null` for users who<br>are using gravatar as their avatar. This option<br>significantly reduces the compressed size of user data,<br>since gravatar URLs are long, random strings and thus do not<br>compress well. The `client_gravatar` field is set to `true` if<br>clients can compute their own gravatars.<br><br>**Changes**: The default value of this parameter was `false`<br>prior to Zulip 5.0 (feature level 92).<br>|
|apply_markdown|query|boolean|false|If `true`, message content is returned in the rendered HTML<br>format. If `false`, message content is returned in the raw<br>Markdown-format text that user entered.<br><br>See [Markdown message formatting](/api/message-formatting) for details on Zulip's HTML format.<br>|
|use_first_unread_anchor|query|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Legacy way to specify `"anchor": "first_unread"` in Zulip 2.1.x and older.<br><br>Whether to use the (computed by the server) first unread message<br>matching the narrow as the `anchor`. Mutually exclusive with `anchor`.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1) and replaced by<br>`"anchor": "first_unread"`.<br>|
|message_ids|query|[integer]|false|A list of message IDs to fetch. The server will return messages corresponding to the<br>subset of the requested message IDs that exist and the current user has access to,<br>potentially filtered by the narrow (if that parameter is provided).<br><br>It is an error to pass this parameter as well as any of the parameters involved in<br>specifying a range of messages: `anchor`, `include_anchor`, `use_first_unread_anchor`,<br>`num_before`, and `num_after`.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 300). Previously, there was<br>no way to request a specific set of messages IDs.<br>|
|allow_empty_topic_name|query|boolean|false|Whether the client supports processing the empty string as a topic in the<br>topic name fields in the returned data, including in returned edit_history data.<br><br>If `false`, the server will use the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name`<br>found in the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) response instead of empty string<br>to represent the empty string topic in its response.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334). Previously, the empty string<br>was not a valid topic.<br>|

> Example responses

<h3 id="get-messages-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|msg|string|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|[IgnoredParametersUnsupported](#schemaignoredparametersunsupported)|false|none|An array of any parameters sent in the request that are not<br>supported by the endpoint.<br><br>See [error handling](/api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters) documentation<br>for details on this and its change history.<br>|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|msg|object|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|object|false|none|none|
|anchor|integer|false|none|The same `anchor` specified in the request (or the computed one, if<br>`use_first_unread_anchor` is `true`).<br><br>Only present if `message_ids` is not provided.<br>|
|found_newest|boolean|false|none|Whether the server promises that the `messages` list includes the very<br>newest messages matching the narrow (used by clients that paginate their<br>requests to decide whether there may be more messages to fetch).<br>|
|found_oldest|boolean|false|none|Whether the server promises that the `messages` list includes the very<br>oldest messages matching the narrow (used by clients that paginate their<br>requests to decide whether there may be more messages to fetch).<br>|
|found_anchor|boolean|false|none|Whether the anchor message is included in the<br>response. If the message with the ID specified<br>in the request does not exist, did not match<br>the narrow, or was excluded via<br>`"include_anchor": false`, this will be false.<br>|
|history_limited|boolean|false|none|Whether the message history was limited due to<br>plan restrictions. This flag is set to `true`<br>only when the oldest messages(`found_oldest`)<br>matching the narrow is fetched.<br>|
|messages|[object]|true|none|An array of `message` objects.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 3.1 (feature level 26), the<br>`sender_short_name` field was removed from message<br>objects.<br>|
|» avatar_url|string \| null|false|none|The URL of the message sender's avatar. Can be `null` only if<br>the current user has access to the sender's real email address<br>and `client_gravatar` was `true`.<br><br>If `null`, then the sender has not uploaded an avatar in Zulip,<br>and the client can compute the gravatar URL by hashing the<br>sender's email address, which corresponds in this case to their<br>real email address.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 7.0 (feature level 163), access to a<br>user's real email address was a realm-level setting. As of this<br>feature level, `email_address_visibility` is a user setting.<br>|
|» client|string|false|none|A Zulip "client" string, describing what Zulip client<br>sent the message.<br>|
|» content|string|false|none|The content/body of the message.<br>When `apply_markdown` is set, it will be in HTML format.<br><br>See [Markdown message formatting](/api/message-formatting) for details on Zulip's HTML format.<br>|

This<br>will be `text/html` or `text/x-markdown`, depending on<br>whether `apply_markdown` was set.<br><br>See the help center article on [message formatting](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown) for details on Zulip-flavored Markdown.<br>|

|» edit_history|[object]|false|none|An array of objects, with each object documenting the<br>changes in a previous edit made to the message,<br>ordered chronologically from most recent to least recent<br>edit.<br><br>Not present if the message has never been edited or moved,<br>or if [viewing message edit history][edit-history-access]<br>is not allowed in the organization.<br><br>Every object will contain `user_id` and `timestamp`.<br><br>The other fields are optional, and will be present or not<br>depending on whether the channel, topic, and/or message<br>content were modified in the edit event. For example, if<br>only the topic was edited, only `prev_topic` and `topic`<br>will be present in addition to `user_id` and `timestamp`.<br><br>[edit-history-access]: /help/restrict-message-edit-history-access<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 10.0 (feature level 284), removed the<br>`prev_rendered_content_version` field as it is an internal<br>server implementation detail not used by any client.<br>|
|» » prev_content|string|false|none|Only present if message's content was edited.<br><br>The content of the message immediately prior to this<br>edit event.<br>|

Previously,<br>parsing the `edit_history` array was required in order to correctly<br>display moved message indicators.<br>|

## Send a message

<a id="opIdsend-message"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'type=direct&to=%5B9%2C10%5D&content=Hello&topic=Castle&queue_id=fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8&local_id=100.01&read_by_sender=true'
```

`POST /messages`

Send a [channel message](/help/introduction-to-topics) or a
[direct message](/help/direct-messages).


> Body parameter

```yaml
type: direct
to:
  - 9
  - 10
content: Hello
topic: Castle
queue_id: fb67bf8a-c031-47cc-84cf-ed80accacda8
local_id: "100.01"
read_by_sender: true
```

<h3 id="send-a-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of message to be sent.<br><br>`"direct"` for a direct message and `"stream"` or `"channel"` for a<br>channel message.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 9.0 (feature level 248), `"channel"` was added as<br>an additional value for this parameter to request a channel message.<br><br>In Zulip 7.0 (feature level 174), `"direct"` was added as<br>the preferred way to request a direct message, deprecating the original<br>`"private"`. While `"private"` is still supported for requesting direct<br>messages, clients are encouraged to use to the modern convention with<br>servers that support it, because support for `"private"` will eventually<br>be removed.<br>|
|» to|body|string \| integer \| [string] \| [integer]|true|The channel or users receiving the message.<br><br>For channel messages, this is either the name or integer ID of the<br>channel.<br><br>For direct messages, this is either a list containing integer user IDs or<br>a list containing string Zulip API email addresses. The ID or email<br>address of the user sending the message can be included in the list, but<br>will be ignored by the server, unless the user sending the message is the<br>only recipient of the message.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 2.0.0, support for using user/channel IDs was added.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[integer]|false|none|
|» content|body|[RequiredContent](#schemarequiredcontent)|true|The content of the message.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_message_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum message size.<br>|
|» topic|body|string|false|The topic of the message. Only required for channel messages<br>(`"type": "stream"` or `"type": "channel"`), ignored otherwise.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_topic_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum topic length.<br><br>Note: When `"(no topic)"` or the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name`<br>found in the [POST /register](/api/register-queue) response is used for this<br>parameter, it is interpreted as an empty string.<br><br>When [topics are required](/help/require-topics), this parameter can't<br>be `"(no topic)"`, an empty string, or the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name`.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 370), `"(no topic)"`<br>was not interpreted as an empty string.<br><br>Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334), empty string<br>was not a valid topic name for channel messages.<br><br>New in Zulip 2.0.0. Previous Zulip releases encoded<br>this as `subject`, which is currently a deprecated alias.<br>|
|» queue_id|body|string|false|For clients supporting<br>[local echo](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/sending-messages.html#local-echo),<br>the [event queue](/api/register-queue) ID for the client.<br><br>If passed, `local_id` is required.<br><br>If the message is successfully sent, the server will include<br>`local_message_id` in the [`message` event](/api/get-events#message) that<br>the client with this `queue_id` will receive.<br>|
|» local_id|body|string|false|For clients supporting<br>[local echo](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/sending-messages.html#local-echo),<br>a unique string-format identifier chosen freely by the client.<br><br>If passed, `queue_id` is required.<br><br>If the message is successfully sent, the server will pass it back to<br>the client without inspecting it as `local_message_id` in the<br>[`message` event](/api/get-events#message) that the client with the<br>above `queue_id` will receive.<br>|
|» read_by_sender|body|boolean|false|Whether the message should be initially marked read by its<br>sender. If unspecified, the server uses a heuristic based<br>on the client name.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 236).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|direct|
|» type|channel|
|» type|stream|
|» type|private|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "id": 42,
  "message_url": "https://example.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/7-test-here/topic/test/near/42",
  "message_link": "[#test here > test @ 💬](https://example.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/7-test-here/topic/test/near/42)",
  "automatic_new_visibility_policy": 2
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Channel 'nonexistent' does not exist",
  "code": "STREAM_DOES_NOT_EXIST",
  "stream": "nonexistent"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-message-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

<h3 id="send-a-message-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|msg|string|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|[IgnoredParametersUnsupported](#schemaignoredparametersunsupported)|false|none|An array of any parameters sent in the request that are not<br>supported by the endpoint.<br><br>See [error handling](/api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters) documentation<br>for details on this and its change history.<br>|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|msg|object|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|object|false|none|none|
|id|integer|true|none|The unique ID assigned to the sent message.<br>|
|message_url|string|true|none|A URL that [links directly to the sent<br>message](/help/link-to-a-message-or-conversation#get-a-link-to-a-specific-message)<br>within its conversation.<br><br>For channel messages, [the channel's name is included in the<br>URL](/api/zulip-urls#encoding-channels) only when the sender has access to<br>the channel's metadata. Otherwise, a URL referencing the channel by ID alone<br>is returned, so that the channel's name is not revealed to a sender who<br>cannot otherwise access it (such as a bot with permission to post to the<br>channel but not to read it).<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 508).<br>|
|message_link|string|true|none|A [Markdown link](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown#links) to the<br>sent message within its conversation, matching the link produced by the<br>["Copy link to<br>message"](/help/link-to-a-message-or-conversation#get-a-link-to-a-specific-message)<br>feature in the Zulip web app; for example,<br>`[#channel name > topic name @ 💬](message_url)`.<br><br>For direct messages, and for channel messages where the channel name is<br>omitted from `message_url` as described above, this is the same plain URL as<br>`message_url` since there is no suitable text label for the Markdown link<br>formatting.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 508).<br>|
|automatic_new_visibility_policy|integer|false|none|If the message's sender had configured their [visibility policy settings](/help/mute-a-topic)<br>to potentially automatically follow or unmute topics when sending messages,<br>and one of these policies did in fact change the user's visibility policy<br>for the topic where this message was sent, the new value for that user's<br>visibility policy for the recipient topic.<br><br>Only present if the sender's visibility was in fact changed.<br><br>The value can be either [unmuted or followed](/api/update-user-topic#parameter-visibility_policy).<br><br>Clients will also be notified about the change in policy via a<br>`user_topic` event as usual. This field is intended to be used by clients<br>to explicitly inform the user when a topic's visibility policy was changed<br>automatically due to sending a message.<br><br>For example, the Zulip web application uses this field to decide whether<br>to display a warning or notice suggesting to unmute the topic after<br>sending a message to a muted channel. Such a notice would be confusing in<br>the event that the act of sending the message had already resulted in the<br>user automatically unmuting or following the topic in question.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 218).<br>|

## Get a message's edit history

<a id="opIdget-message-history"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/43/history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /messages/{message_id}/history`

Fetch the message edit history of a previously edited message.

Note that edit history may be disabled in some organizations; see the
[Zulip help center documentation on editing messages][edit-settings].

[edit-settings]: /help/view-a-messages-edit-history


<h3 id="get-a-messages-edit-history-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message_id|path|integer|true|The target message's ID.<br>|
|allow_empty_topic_name|query|boolean|false|Whether the topic names i.e. `topic` and `prev_topic` fields in<br>the `message_history` objects returned can be empty string.<br><br>If `false`, the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name`<br>found in the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) response is<br>returned replacing the empty string as the topic name.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334).<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "message_history": [
    {
      "content": "Hello!",
      "topic": "party at my houz",
      "rendered_content": "<p>Hello!</p>",
      "timestamp": 1530129122,
      "user_id": 5
    },
    {
      "topic": "party at my house",
      "content": "Howdy!",
      "prev_content": "Hello!",
      "rendered_content": "<p>Howdy!</p>",
      "user_id": 5,
      "prev_rendered_content": "<p>Hello!</p>",
      "content_html_diff": "<div><p><span class=\"highlight_text_inserted\">Howdy!</span></p> <p><span class=\"highlight_text_deleted\">Hello!</span></p></div>",
      "prev_topic": "party at my houz",
      "timestamp": 1530129134
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Invalid message(s)",
  "code": "BAD_REQUEST"
}
```

<h3 id="get-a-messages-edit-history-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-a-messages-edit-history-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

## Update personal message flags

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/flags \

  -d 'messages=%5B4%2C8%2C15%5D&op=add&flag=read'
```

`POST /messages/flags`

Add or remove personal message flags like `read` and `starred`
on a collection of message IDs.

messages within a narrow](/api/update-message-flags-for-narrow).

```yaml
  - 8
```

|» op|body|string|true|Whether to `add` the flag or `remove` it.<br>|
|» flag|body|string|true|The flag that should be added/removed.<br>|

|» op|remove|

## Update personal message flags for narrow

<a id="opIdupdate-message-flags-for-narrow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/flags/narrow \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'anchor=%7B%7D&include_anchor=false&num_before=4&num_after=8&narrow=%5B%7B%22operand%22%3A%22Denmark%22%2C%22operator%22%3A%22channel%22%7D%5D&op=add&flag=read'
```

`POST /messages/flags/narrow`

Add or remove personal message flags like `read` and `starred`
on a range of messages within a narrow.

See also [the endpoint for updating flags on specific message
IDs](/api/update-message-flags).

**Changes**: New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 155).


> Body parameter

```yaml
anchor: {}
include_anchor: false
num_before: 4
num_after: 8
narrow:
  -
    operand: Denmark
    operator: channel
op: add
flag: read
```

<h3 id="update-personal-message-flags-for-narrow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|body|body|object|true|none|

|» num_before|body|integer|true|Limit the number of messages preceding the anchor in the<br>update range. The server may decrease this to bound<br>transaction sizes.<br>|
|» num_after|body|integer|true|Limit the number of messages following the anchor in the<br>update range. The server may decrease this to bound<br>transaction sizes.<br>|
|» narrow|body|[object \| [string]]|true|The narrow you want update flags within. See how to<br>[construct a narrow](/api/construct-narrow).<br><br>Note that, when adding the `read` flag to messages, clients should<br>consider including a narrow with the `is:unread` filter as an<br>optimization. Including that filter takes advantage of the fact that<br>the server has a database index for unread messages.<br><br>**Changes**: See [changes section](/api/construct-narrow#changes)<br>of search/narrow filter documentation.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » operator|body|string|true|none|
|» » operand|body|string \| integer \| [integer]|true|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|body|[integer]|false|none|
|» » negated|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» op|body|string|true|Whether to `add` the flag or `remove` it.<br>|
|» flag|body|string|true|The flag that should be added/removed. See [available<br>flags](/api/update-message-flags#available-flags).<br>|

## Render a message

<a id="opIdrender-message"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/render \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'content=Hello&populate_url_embed_data=true'
```

`POST /messages/render`

Render a message to HTML.


> Body parameter

```yaml
content: Hello
populate_url_embed_data: true
```

<h3 id="render-a-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» content|body|[RequiredContent](#schemarequiredcontent)|true|The content of the message.<br><br>Clients should use the `max_message_length` returned by the<br>[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) endpoint to determine<br>the maximum message size.<br>|
|» populate_url_embed_data|body|boolean|false|Whether the server should populate<br>[URL embed data](/help/image-video-and-website-previews)<br>for the links in `content`: data the server already has is<br>included in `rendered`, and the rest is fetched<br>asynchronously. If that changes the rendered content, it is<br>delivered to the requesting user via a<br>[`url_embed_data` event](/api/get-events#url_embed_data), so<br>that a client displaying the rendered content can live-update<br>it. See the event's documentation for when it is not sent.<br><br>Only links that would get URL embeds if `content` were sent<br>as a message are populated. For example, links to websites<br>are not populated for bots, or if the organization has<br>disabled website previews.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 513).<br>|

## Add an emoji reaction

<a id="opIdadd-reaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/43/reactions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'emoji_name=octopus&emoji_code=1f419&reaction_type=unicode_emoji'
```

`POST /messages/{message_id}/reactions`

Add an [emoji reaction](/help/emoji-reactions) to a message.


> Body parameter

```yaml
emoji_name: octopus
emoji_code: "1f419"
reaction_type: unicode_emoji
```

<h3 id="add-an-emoji-reaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message_id|path|integer|true|The target message's ID.<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» emoji_name|body|string|true|The target emoji's human-readable name.<br><br>To find an emoji's name, hover over a message to reveal<br>three icons on the right, then click the smiley face icon.<br>Images of available reaction emojis appear. Hover over the<br>emoji you want, and note that emoji's text name.<br>|
|» emoji_code|body|[EmojiCode](#schemaemojicode)|false|A unique identifier, defining the specific emoji codepoint requested,<br>within the namespace of the `reaction_type`.<br><br>For most API clients, you won't need this, but it's important<br>for Zulip apps to handle rare corner cases when<br>adding/removing votes on an emoji reaction added previously by<br>another user.<br><br>If the existing reaction was added when the Zulip server was<br>using a previous version of the emoji data mapping between<br>Unicode codepoints and human-readable names, sending the<br>`emoji_code` in the data for the original reaction allows the<br>Zulip server to correctly interpret your upvote as an upvote<br>rather than a reaction with a "different" emoji.<br>|
|» reaction_type|body|[ReactionType](#schemareactiontype)|false|A string indicating the type of emoji. Each emoji `reaction_type`<br>has an independent namespace for values of `emoji_code`.<br><br>If an API client is adding/removing a vote on an existing reaction,<br>it should pass this parameter using the value the server provided<br>for the existing reaction for specificity. Supported values:<br><br>- `unicode_emoji` : In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be a<br>  dash-separated hex encoding of the sequence of Unicode codepoints<br>  that define this emoji in the Unicode specification.<br><br>- `realm_emoji` : In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be the ID of<br>  the uploaded [custom emoji](/help/custom-emoji).<br><br>- `zulip_extra_emoji` : These are special emoji included with Zulip.<br>  In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be the name of the emoji (e.g.<br>  "zulip").<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 3.0 (feature level 2), this parameter became<br>optional for [custom emoji](/help/custom-emoji);<br>previously, this endpoint assumed `unicode_emoji` if this<br>parameter was not specified.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "result": "error",
  "msg": "Invalid emoji code",
  "code": "BAD_REQUEST"
}
```

<h3 id="add-an-emoji-reaction-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|[JsonSuccess](#schemajsonsuccess)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request.|Inline|

## Get a message's read receipts

<a id="opIdget-read-receipts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/43/read_receipts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /messages/{message_id}/read_receipts`

Returns a list containing the IDs for all users who have
marked the message as read (and whose privacy settings allow
sharing that information).

The list of users IDs will include any bots who have marked
the message as read via the API (providing a way for bots to
indicate whether they have processed a message successfully in
a way that can be easily inspected in a Zulip client). Bots
for which this behavior is not desired may disable the
`send_read_receipts` setting via the API.

It will never contain the message's sender.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 137).


<h3 id="get-a-messages-read-receipts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

## Check if messages match a narrow

<a id="opIdcheck-messages-match-narrow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/matches_narrow?msg_ids=%5B0%5D&narrow=%5B%7B%7D%5D' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /messages/matches_narrow`

Check whether a set of messages match a [narrow](/api/construct-narrow).

For many common narrows (e.g. a topic), clients can write an efficient
client-side check to determine whether a newly arrived message belongs
in the view.

This endpoint is designed to allow clients to handle more complex narrows
for which the client does not (or in the case of full-text search, cannot)
implement this check.

The format of the `match_subject` and `match_content` objects is designed
to match those returned by the [`GET /messages`](/api/get-messages#response)
endpoint, so that a client can splice these fields into a `message` object
received from [`GET /events`](/api/get-events#message) and end up with an
extended message object identical to how a [`GET /messages`](/api/get-messages)
request for the current narrow would have returned the message.


<h3 id="check-if-messages-match-a-narrow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|msg_ids|query|[integer]|true|List of IDs for the messages to check.|
|narrow|query|[object]|true|A structure defining the narrow to check against. See how to<br>[construct a narrow](/api/construct-narrow).<br><br>**Changes**: See [changes section](/api/construct-narrow#changes)<br>of search/narrow filter documentation.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
    "string"
  ],
  "messages": {
    "31": {
      "match_content": "<p><a href=\"http://foo.com\" target=\"_blank\" title=\"http://foo.com\">http://foo.com</a></p>",
      "match_subject": "test_topic"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="check-if-messages-match-a-narrow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success.|Inline|

<h3 id="check-if-messages-match-a-narrow-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|result|string|true|none|none|
|msg|string|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|[IgnoredParametersUnsupported](#schemaignoredparametersunsupported)|false|none|An array of any parameters sent in the request that are not<br>supported by the endpoint.<br><br>See [error handling](/api/rest-error-handling#ignored-parameters) documentation<br>for details on this and its change history.<br>|
|result|object|true|none|none|
|msg|object|true|none|none|
|ignored_parameters_unsupported|object|false|none|none|
|messages|object|false|none|A dictionary with a key for each queried message that matches the narrow,<br>with message IDs as keys and search rendering data as values.<br>|
|» **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|`message_id`: The ID of the message that matches the narrow. No record will be returned<br>for queried messages that do not match the narrow.<br>|
|» » match_content|string|false|none|HTML content of a queried message that matches the narrow. If the<br>narrow is a search narrow, `<span class="highlight">` elements<br>will be included, wrapping the matches for the search keywords.<br>|
|» » match_subject|string|false|none|HTML-escaped topic of a queried message that matches the narrow. If the<br>narrow is a search narrow, `<span class="highlight">` elements<br>will be included wrapping the matches for the search keywords.<br>|

## Fetch a single message

<a id="opIdget-message"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/43 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /messages/{message_id}`

Given a message ID, return the message object.

Additionally, a `raw_content` field is included. This field is
useful for clients that primarily work with HTML-rendered
messages but might need to occasionally fetch the message's
raw [Zulip-flavored Markdown](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown) (e.g. for [view
source](/help/view-the-markdown-source-of-a-message) or
prefilling a message edit textarea).

**Changes**: Before Zulip 5.0 (feature level 120), this
endpoint only returned the `raw_content` field.


<h3 id="fetch-a-single-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message_id|path|integer|true|The target message's ID.<br>|
|apply_markdown|query|boolean|false|If `true`, message content is returned in the rendered HTML<br>format. If `false`, message content is returned in the raw<br>[Zulip-flavored Markdown format](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown) text that user entered.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 5.0 (feature level 120).<br>|
|allow_empty_topic_name|query|boolean|false|Whether the client supports processing the empty string as a topic in the<br>topic name fields in the returned data, including in returned edit_history data.<br><br>If `false`, the server will use the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name`<br>found in the [`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) response instead of empty string<br>to represent the empty string topic in its response.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334). Previously, the empty string<br>was not a valid topic.<br>|

## Delete a message

<a id="opIddelete-message"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.zulipchat.com/api/v1/messages/43 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /messages/{message_id}`

Permanently delete a message.

This API corresponds to the [delete a message completely][delete-completely]
feature documented in the Zulip help center.

A user must be able to access the content of a message in order to delete it.
See [channel permissions](/help/channel-permissions) for more information
about content access for channel messages. For direct messages, the user
must have received or sent the direct message to have content access.

See [restricting message deletion](/help/restrict-message-editing-and-deletion)
for documentation on when users are allowed to delete messages.

The relevant realm settings in the API that are related to the above linked
documentation on when users are allowed to delete messages are:

- `realm_can_delete_any_message_group`
- `realm_can_delete_own_message_group`
- `realm_can_set_delete_message_policy_group`
- `realm_message_content_delete_limit_seconds`

The relevant per-channel permission settings in the API that are related to the
above linked documentation on when users are allowed to delete messages in a
specific channel are:

- `can_delete_any_message_group`
- `can_delete_own_message_group`

More details about these realm and channel settings can be found in the
[`POST /register`](/api/register-queue) response.

**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 10.0 (feature level 281), only organization
administrators had permission to permanently delete a message.

[delete-completely]: /help/delete-a-message#delete-a-message-completely


<h3 id="delete-a-message-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|message_id|path|integer|true|The target message's ID.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": "success",
  "msg": "",
  "ignored_parameters_unsupported": [
```
