Dictionary containing details of a file uploaded by a user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|The unique ID for the attachment.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|Name of the uploaded file.<br>|
|path_id|string|false|none|A representation of the path of the file within the<br>repository of user-uploaded files. If the `path_id` of a<br>file is `{realm_id}/ab/cdef/temp_file.py`, its URL will be:<br>`{server_url}/user_uploads/{realm_id}/ab/cdef/temp_file.py`.<br>|
|size|integer|false|none|Size of the file in bytes.<br>|
|create_time|integer|false|none|Time when the attachment was uploaded as a UNIX timestamp.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 12.0 (feature level 443), this value<br>was milliseconds since the epoch, not seconds.<br><br>Changed in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 22). This field was<br>previously a floating point number.<br>|
|message_ids|[integer]|false|none|Array containing the IDs of messages that reference this<br>[uploaded file](/api/upload-file). This includes messages<br>sent by any user in the Zulip organization who sent a<br>message containing a link to the uploaded file.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 12.0 (feature level 472), this<br>replaced the previous `messages` field, which was an array<br>of objects containing both `id` and `date_sent` properties.<br>|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_id|integer|true|none|The unique ID of the channel.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the channel.<br>|
|is_archived|boolean|true|none|A boolean indicating whether the channel is [archived](/help/archive-a-channel).<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 315).<br>Previously, this endpoint never returned archived channels.<br>|
|description|string|true|none|The short description of the channel in [Zulip-flavored Markdown](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown) format,<br>intended to be used to prepopulate UI for editing a channel's<br>description.<br><br>See [Markdown message formatting](/api/message-formatting) for details on Zulip's HTML format.<br>|
|date_created|integer|true|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the channel was created, in UTC seconds.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 30).<br>|
|creator_id|integer \| null|true|none|The ID of the user who created this channel.<br><br>A `null` value means the channel has no recorded creator, which is often<br>because the channel is very old, was created during realm creation or<br>because it was created via a data import tool or [management command][management-commands].<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 9.0 (feature level 254).<br><br>[management-commands]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/management-commands.html<br>|
|invite_only|boolean|true|none|Specifies whether the channel is private or not.<br>Only people who have been invited can access a private channel.<br>|
|rendered_description|string|true|none|The short description of the channel rendered as HTML, intended to<br>be used when displaying the channel description in a UI.<br><br>One should use the standard Zulip rendered_markdown CSS when<br>displaying this content so that emoji, LaTeX, and other syntax<br>work correctly. And any client-side security logic for<br>user-generated message content should be applied when displaying<br>this HTML as though it were the body of a Zulip message.<br>|
|is_web_public|boolean|true|none|Whether the channel has been configured to allow unauthenticated<br>access to its message history from the web.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 2.1.0.<br>|
|stream_post_policy|integer|true|none|**Deprecated.** A deprecated representation of a superset of the users who<br>have permission to post messages to the channel available<br>for backwards-compatibility. Clients should use<br>`can_send_message_group` instead.<br><br>It is an enum with the following possible values, corresponding<br>to roles/system groups:<br><br>- 1 = Any user can post.<br>- 2 = Only administrators can post.<br>- 3 = Only [full members][calc-full-member] can post.<br>- 4 = Only moderators can post.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 333) and<br>replaced by `can_send_message_group`, which supports finer<br>resolution of configurations, resulting in this property being<br>inaccurate following that transition.<br><br>New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1), replacing the previous<br>`is_announcement_only` boolean.<br><br>[calc-full-member]: /api/roles-and-permissions#determining-if-a-user-is-a-full-member<br>|
|message_retention_days|integer \| null|true|none|Number of days that messages sent to this channel will be stored<br>before being automatically deleted by the [message retention<br>policy](/help/message-retention-policy). There are two special values:<br><br>- `null`, the default, means the channel will inherit the organization<br>  level setting.<br>- `-1` encodes retaining messages in this channel forever.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 17).<br>|
|default_push_notifications|[DefaultPushNotifications](#schemadefaultpushnotifications)|true|none|Whether mobile push notifications will be enabled by default when a<br>user first subscribes to this channel, potentially overriding the<br>user's [default mobile notification<br>setting](/help/channel-notifications#configure-default-notifications-for-all-channels)<br>for channel messages.<br><br>Because this default is applied only the first time a user<br>subscribes, unsubscribing and resubscribing a user does not reset<br>their preference to this channel default.<br><br>Only organization administrators can set or modify this value.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 507).<br>|
|history_public_to_subscribers|boolean|true|none|Whether the history of the channel is public to its subscribers.<br><br>Currently always true for public channels (i.e. `"invite_only": false` implies<br>`"history_public_to_subscribers": true`), but clients should not make that<br>assumption, as we may change that behavior in the future.<br>|
|topics_policy|[TopicsPolicy](#schematopicspolicy)|false|none|Whether [named topics](/help/introduction-to-topics) and the empty<br>topic (i.e., ["general chat" topic](/help/general-chat-topic))<br>are enabled in this channel.<br><br>- `"inherit"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this channel,<br>  and the [organization-level `realm_topics_policy`][realm-topics-policy]<br>  is used for whether messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel.<br>- `"allow_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to both named topics and<br>  the empty topic in this channel.<br>- `"disable_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this<br>  channel, but the empty topic is disabled.<br>- `"empty_topic_only"`: Messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel, but named topics are disabled. See ["general chat"<br>  channels](/help/general-chat-channels).<br><br>The `"empty_topic_only"` policy can only be set if all existing messages<br>in the channel are already in the empty topic.<br><br>When creating a new channel, if the `topics_policy` is not specified, the<br>`"inherit"` option will be set.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 11.0 (feature level 404), the `"empty_topic_only"`<br>option was added.<br><br>New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 392).<br><br>[realm-topics-policy]: /help/require-topics#set-the-default-general-chat-topic-configuration<br>|
|first_message_id|integer \| null|true|none|The ID of the first message in the channel.<br><br>Intended to help clients determine whether they need to display<br>UI like the "show all topics" widget that would suggest the channel<br>has older history that can be accessed.<br><br>Is `null` for channels with no message history.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 2.1.0.<br>|
|folder_id|[FolderId](#schemafolderid)|true|none|The ID of the folder to which the channel belongs.<br><br>Is `null` if channel does not belong to any folder.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 389).<br>|
|is_recently_active|boolean|true|none|Whether the channel has recent message activity. Previously, clients implemented the<br>demote_inactive_streams from local message history, resulting in a choppy loading<br>experience.<br>|
|is_announcement_only|boolean|true|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the given channel is announcement only or not.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). Clients<br>should use `stream_post_policy` instead.<br>|
|can_add_subscribers_group|[ChannelCanAddSubscribersGroup](#schemachannelcanaddsubscribersgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_remove_subscribers_group|[CanRemoveSubscribersGroup](#schemacanremovesubscribersgroup)|true|none|none|
|can_administer_channel_group|[CanAdministerChannelGroup](#schemacanadministerchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_delete_any_message_group|[CanDeleteAnyMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteanymessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_delete_own_message_group|[CanDeleteOwnMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteownmessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group|[CanMoveMessagesOutOfChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessagesoutofchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_move_messages_within_channel_group|[CanMoveMessagesWithinChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessageswithinchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_send_message_group|[CanSendMessageGroup](#schemacansendmessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_subscribe_group|[CanSubscribeGroup](#schemacansubscribegroup)|true|none|none|
|can_resolve_topics_group|[CanResolveTopicsGroup](#schemacanresolvetopicsgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_create_topic_group|[CanCreateTopicGroup](#schemacancreatetopicgroup)|false|none|none|
|subscriber_count|number|true|none|The total number of non-deactivated users (including bots) who<br>are subscribed to the channel. Clients are responsible for updating<br>this value using `peer_add` and `peer_remove` events.<br><br>The server's internals cannot guarantee this value is correctly<br>synced with `peer_add` and `peer_remove` events for the channel. As<br>a result, if a (rare) race occurs between a change in the channel's<br>subscribers and fetching this value, it is possible for a client<br>that is correctly following the events protocol to end up with a<br>permanently off-by-one error in the channel's subscriber count.<br><br>Clients are recommended to fetch full subscriber data for a channel<br>in contexts where it is important to avoid this risk. The official<br>web application, for example, uses this field primarily while<br>waiting to fetch a given channel's full subscriber list from the<br>server.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 394).<br>|

|is_archived|object|true|none|none|

|first_message_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the first message in the channel.<br><br>Intended to help clients determine whether they need to display<br>UI like the "show all topics" widget that would suggest the channel<br>has older history that can be accessed.<br><br>Is `null` for channels with no message history.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 2.1.0.<br>|
|folder_id|[FolderId](#schemafolderid)|false|none|The ID of the folder to which the channel belongs.<br><br>Is `null` if channel does not belong to any folder.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 389).<br>|
|is_recently_active|boolean|false|none|Whether the channel has recent message activity. Clients should use this to implement<br>[hide inactive channels](/help/manage-inactive-channels) if<br>`demote_inactive_streams` is enabled.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 323). Previously, clients implemented the<br>demote_inactive_streams from local message history, resulting in a choppy loading<br>experience.<br>|
|is_announcement_only|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the given channel is announcement only or not.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). Clients<br>should use `stream_post_policy` instead.<br>|
|can_add_subscribers_group|[ChannelCanAddSubscribersGroup](#schemachannelcanaddsubscribersgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_remove_subscribers_group|[CanRemoveSubscribersGroup](#schemacanremovesubscribersgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_administer_channel_group|[CanAdministerChannelGroup](#schemacanadministerchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_delete_any_message_group|[CanDeleteAnyMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteanymessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_delete_own_message_group|[CanDeleteOwnMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteownmessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group|[CanMoveMessagesOutOfChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessagesoutofchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_move_messages_within_channel_group|[CanMoveMessagesWithinChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessageswithinchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_send_message_group|[CanSendMessageGroup](#schemacansendmessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_subscribe_group|[CanSubscribeGroup](#schemacansubscribegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_resolve_topics_group|[CanResolveTopicsGroup](#schemacanresolvetopicsgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_create_topic_group|[CanCreateTopicGroup](#schemacancreatetopicgroup)|false|none|none|
|subscriber_count|number|false|none|The total number of non-deactivated users (including bots) who<br>are subscribed to the channel. Clients are responsible for updating<br>this value using `peer_add` and `peer_remove` events.<br><br>The server's internals cannot guarantee this value is correctly<br>synced with `peer_add` and `peer_remove` events for the channel. As<br>a result, if a (rare) race occurs between a change in the channel's<br>subscribers and fetching this value, it is possible for a client<br>that is correctly following the events protocol to end up with a<br>permanently off-by-one error in the channel's subscriber count.<br><br>Clients are recommended to fetch full subscriber data for a channel<br>in contexts where it is important to avoid this risk. The official<br>web application, for example, uses this field primarily while<br>waiting to fetch a given channel's full subscriber list from the<br>server.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 394).<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|topics_policy|inherit|
|topics_policy|allow_empty_topic|
|topics_policy|disable_empty_topic|
|topics_policy|empty_topic_only|

<h2 id="tocS_WebhookConfigOption">WebhookConfigOption</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawebhookconfigoption"></a>
<a id="schema_WebhookConfigOption"></a>
<a id="tocSwebhookconfigoption"></a>
<a id="tocswebhookconfigoption"></a>

```json
[
  {
    "key": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "validator": "string"
  }
]
```

An array of configuration options that can be set when creating
a bot user for this incoming webhook integration.

This is an unstable API. Please discuss in chat.zulip.org before
using it.

**Changes**: As of Zulip 11.0 (feature level 403), this
object is reserved for integration-specific configuration options
that can be set when creating a bot user. Previously, this object
also included optional webhook URL parameters, which are now
specified in the `url_options` object.

Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 318), this field was named `config`,
and was reserved for configuration data key-value pairs.

```json
[
  {
    "key": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "input_type": "string"
  }
]
```

An array of optional URL parameter options for the incoming webhook
integration. In the web app, these are used when
[generating a URL for an integration](/help/generate-integration-url).

**Changes**: Before Zulip 12.0 (feature level 485), `input_type`
was named `validator`.

New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 403). Previously, these optional
URL parameter options were included in the `config_options` object.

<h2 id="tocS_CustomProfileField">CustomProfileField</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomprofilefield"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomProfileField"></a>
<a id="tocScustomprofilefield"></a>
<a id="tocscustomprofilefield"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "type": 0,
  "order": 0,
  "name": "string",
  "hint": "string",
  "field_data": "string",
  "display_in_profile_summary": false,
  "required": true,
  "editable_by_user": true,
  "use_for_user_matching": false
}
```

Dictionary containing the details of a custom profile field configured
for this organization.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|true|none|The ID of the custom profile field. This will be referenced in the custom<br>profile fields section of user objects.<br>|
|type|integer|true|none|An integer indicating the type of the custom profile field, which determines<br>how it is configured and displayed to users.<br><br>See the [Custom profile fields](/help/custom-profile-fields#profile-field-types)<br>article for details on what each type means.<br><br>- **1**: Short text<br>- **2**: Paragraph<br>- **3**: Dropdown<br>- **4**: Date<br>- **5**: Link<br>- **6**: Users<br>- **7**: External account<br>- **8**: Pronouns<br><br>**Changes**: Field type `8` added in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 151).<br>|
|order|integer|true|none|Custom profile fields are displayed in both settings UI and<br>UI showing users' profiles in increasing `order`.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the custom profile field.<br>|
|hint|string|true|none|The help text to be displayed for the custom profile field in user-facing<br>settings UI for configuring custom profile fields.<br>|
|field_data|string|false|none|Field types 3 (Dropdown) and 7 (External account) support storing<br>additional configuration for the field type in the `field_data` attribute.<br><br>For field type 3 (Dropdown), this attribute is a JSON object<br>defining the choices and the order they will be displayed in the<br>dropdown UI for individual users to select an option.<br><br>The interface for field type 7 is not yet stabilized.<br>|
|display_in_profile_summary|boolean|false|none|Whether the custom profile field, display or not on the user card.<br><br>Must be false for `Users`<br>[profile field types](/help/custom-profile-fields#profile-field-types).<br><br>This field is only included when its value is `true`.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 12.0 (feature level 476), the<br>"Paragraph" field type was not supported.<br><br>New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 146).<br>|
|required|boolean|true|none|Whether an organization administrator has configured this profile field as<br>required.<br><br>Because the required property is mutable, clients cannot assume that a required<br>custom profile field has a value. The Zulip web application displays a prominent<br>banner to any user who has not set a value for a required field.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 9.0 (feature level 244).<br>|
|editable_by_user|boolean|true|none|Whether regular users can edit this profile field on their own account.<br><br>Note that organization administrators can edit custom profile fields for any user<br>regardless of this setting.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 296).<br>|
|use_for_user_matching|boolean|false|none|Whether this custom profile field should be used to match users in typeahead<br>suggestions. Only allowed for Short Text and External Account<br>[profile field types](/help/custom-profile-fields#profile-field-types).<br><br>This field is only included when its value is `true`.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 455).<br>|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="tocScustomprofilefieldhintschema"></a>

```json
"Your favorite programming language."
```

The help text to be displayed for the custom profile field in user-facing
settings UI for configuring custom profile fields.

<h2 id="tocS_CustomProfileFieldDataSchema">CustomProfileFieldDataSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomprofilefielddataschema"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomProfileFieldDataSchema"></a>
<a id="tocScustomprofilefielddataschema"></a>
<a id="tocscustomprofilefielddataschema"></a>

```json
{
  "python": {
    "text": "Python",
    "order": "1"
  },
  "java": {
    "text": "Java",
    "order": "2"
  }
}
```

Field types 3 (Dropdown) and 7 (External account) support storing
additional configuration for the field type in the `field_data` attribute.

For field type 3 (Dropdown), this attribute is a JSON object
defining the choices and the order they will be displayed in the
dropdown UI for individual users to select an option.

The interface for field type 7 is not yet stabilized.

See [profile field types](/help/custom-profile-fields#profile-field-types)
or the [`field_type` parameter](/api/create-custom-profile-field#parameter-field_type)
for what each field type number means.

<h2 id="tocS_CustomProfileFieldDisplayInProfileSummarySchema">CustomProfileFieldDisplayInProfileSummarySchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomprofilefielddisplayinprofilesummaryschema"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomProfileFieldDisplayInProfileSummarySchema"></a>
<a id="tocScustomprofilefielddisplayinprofilesummaryschema"></a>
<a id="tocscustomprofilefielddisplayinprofilesummaryschema"></a>

```json
true
```

Whether clients should display this profile field in the summary section of a
user's profile (or in a more easily accessible "small profile").

At most 2 profile fields may have this property be true in a given
organization.

The "Users" profile field is not supported, but that is likely to
be temporary.

**Changes**: Before Zulip 12.0 (feature level 476), the
"Paragraph" field type was not supported.

New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 146).

<h2 id="tocS_CustomProfileFieldRequiredSchema">CustomProfileFieldRequiredSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomprofilefieldrequiredschema"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomProfileFieldRequiredSchema"></a>
<a id="tocScustomprofilefieldrequiredschema"></a>
<a id="tocscustomprofilefieldrequiredschema"></a>

```json
true
```

Whether an organization administrator has configured this profile field as
required.

Because the required property is mutable, clients cannot assume that a required
custom profile field has a value. The Zulip web application displays a prominent
banner to any user who has not set a value for a required field.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 9.0 (feature level 244).

<h2 id="tocS_CustomProfileFieldEditableByUserSchema">CustomProfileFieldEditableByUserSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomprofilefieldeditablebyuserschema"></a>

<a id="tocScustomprofilefieldeditablebyuserschema"></a>
<a id="tocscustomprofilefieldeditablebyuserschema"></a>

```json
true
```

Whether regular users can edit this profile field on their own account.

Note that organization administrators can edit custom profile fields for any user
regardless of this setting.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 296).

<h2 id="tocS_CustomProfileFieldUseForUserMatchingSchema">CustomProfileFieldUseForUserMatchingSchema</h2>

<a id="schemacustomprofilefielduseforusermatchingschema"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomProfileFieldUseForUserMatchingSchema"></a>
<a id="tocScustomprofilefielduseforusermatchingschema"></a>
<a id="tocscustomprofilefielduseforusermatchingschema"></a>

```json
false
```

Whether this custom profile field should be used to match users in typeahead
suggestions. Only allowed for Short Text and External Account
[profile field types](/help/custom-profile-fields#profile-field-types).

This field is only included when its value is `true`.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 455).

Object containing details about an emoji. It has the
following properties:

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|id|string|false|none|The ID for this emoji, same as the object's key.<br>|

|source_url|string|false|none|The path relative to the organization's URL where the<br>emoji's image can be found.<br>|
|still_url|string \| null|false|none|Only non-null when the emoji's image is animated.<br><br>The path relative to the organization's URL where a still<br>(not animated) version of the emoji can be found. (This is<br>currently always the first frame of the animation).<br><br>This is useful for clients to display the emoji in contexts<br>where continuously animating it would be a bad user experience<br>(E.g. because it would be distracting).<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 5.0 (added as optional field in<br>feature level 97 and then made mandatory, but nullable, in<br>feature level 113).<br>|
|deactivated|boolean|false|none|Whether the emoji has been deactivated or not.<br>|
|author_id|integer \| null|false|none|The user ID of the user who uploaded the custom emoji.<br>Will be `null` if the uploader is unknown.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 7). Previously<br>was accessible via an `author` object with an `id` field.<br>|

Object containing details about a
[data export](/help/export-your-organization).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|The ID of the data export.<br>|
|acting_user_id|integer|false|none|The ID of the user who created the data export.<br>|
|export_time|number|false|none|The UNIX timestamp of when the data export was started.<br>|
|deleted_timestamp|number \| null|false|none|The UNIX timestamp of when the data export was deleted.<br><br>Will be `null` if the data export has not been deleted.<br>|
|failed_timestamp|number \| null|false|none|The UNIX timestamp of when the data export failed.<br><br>Will be `null` if the data export succeeded, or if it's<br>still being generated.<br>|
|export_url|string \| null|false|none|The URL to download the generated data export.<br><br>Will be `null` if the data export failed, if it's<br>still being generated, or if this export happened<br>on a previous server.<br><br>**Changes**: Starting in Zulip 12.1 (feature levels 499-501, and<br>506+), this is also `null` for exports that happened on a previous<br>server.<br>|
|pending|boolean|false|none|Whether the data export is pending, which indicates it<br>is still being generated, or if it succeeded, failed or<br>was deleted before being generated.<br><br>Depending on the size of the organization, it can take<br>anywhere from seconds to an hour to generate the data<br>export.<br>|
|export_from_prior_server|boolean|false|none|Whether this data export happened on a previous server,<br>and thus its tarball is no longer stored on this server.<br>This is `true` for records that were carried across a<br>realm import; the record is preserved for audit purposes<br>but its data is no longer available for download.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.1 (feature levels 499-501, and 506+).<br>|
|export_type|string|false|none|Whether the data export is public, full with consent, or full without consent.<br><br>- `public` = Public data export.<br>- `full_with_consent` = Public and private data export (with consent), which includes private data<br>  for users who have granted consent.<br>- `full_without_consent` = All public and private data, which includes private data for all users.<br><br>**Changes**: Zulip 12.0 (feature level 449) changed the type of<br>this field from int to string with `1` being replaced by `public` and<br>`2` being replaced by `full_with_consent`. The option `full_without_consent`<br>was added for full exports without member consent.<br><br>New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 304). Previously,<br>the export type was not included in these objects because only<br>public data exports could be created or listed via the API or UI.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|export_type|public|
|export_type|full_with_consent|
|export_type|full_without_consent|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|name|string|false|none|The name of the user group.<br>|
|date_created|integer \| null|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the user group was created, in UTC seconds.<br><br>A `null` value means the user group has no recorded date, which is often<br>because the user group is very old, or because it was created via a data<br>import tool or [management command][management-commands].<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 292).<br>[management-commands]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/management-commands.html<br>|
|creator_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the user who created this user group.<br><br>A `null` value means the user group has no recorded creator, which is often<br>because the user group is very old, or because it was created via a data<br>import tool or [management command][management-commands].<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 292).<br>[management-commands]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/management-commands.html<br>|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the user group.<br>|
|members|[integer]|false|none|Array containing the ID of the users who are<br>members of this user group.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 10.0 (feature level 303), this<br>list also included deactivated users who were members of<br>the user group before being deactivated.<br>|
|direct_subgroup_ids|[integer]|false|none|Array containing the ID of the direct_subgroups of<br>this user group.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 131).<br>Introduced in feature level 127 as `subgroups`, but<br>clients can ignore older events as this feature level<br>predates subgroups being fully implemented.<br>|
|id|integer|false|none|The ID of the user group.<br>|
|is_system_group|boolean|false|none|Whether the user group is a system group which cannot be<br>directly modified by users.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 5.0 (feature level 93).<br>|
|can_add_members_group|object|false|none|none|
|can_join_group|object|false|none|none|
|can_leave_group|object|false|none|none|
|can_manage_group|object|false|none|none|
|can_mention_group|object|false|none|none|
|can_remove_members_group|object|false|none|none|
|deactivated|boolean|false|none|Whether the user group is deactivated. Deactivated groups<br>cannot be used as a subgroup of another group or used for<br>any other purpose.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 290).<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Invite">Invite</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainvite"></a>
<a id="schema_Invite"></a>
<a id="tocSinvite"></a>
<a id="tocsinvite"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "invited_by_user_id": 0,
  "invited": 0,
  "expiry_date": 0,
  "invited_as": 100,
  "email": "string",
  "notify_referrer_on_join": true,
  "link_url": "string",
  "is_multiuse": true
}
```

A dictionary containing details about an [invitation](/help/invite-new-users).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|The ID of the invitation.<br><br>Note that email invitations and reusable invitation links are stored<br>in different database tables on the server, so each ID is guaranteed<br>to be unique in combination with the boolean value of `is_multiuse`,<br>e.g. there can only be one invitation with `id: 1` and `is_multiuse:<br>true`.<br>|
|invited_by_user_id|integer|false|none|The [user ID](/api/get-user) of the user who created the invitation.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 22), replacing the `ref`<br>field which contained the Zulip display email address of the user who<br>created the invitation.<br>|
|invited|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the invitation was created, in UTC seconds.<br>|
|expiry_date|integer \| null|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the invitation will expire, in UTC seconds.<br>If `null`, the invitation never expires.<br>|
|invited_as|integer|false|none|The [organization-level role](/api/roles-and-permissions) of the user that<br>is created when the invitation is accepted.<br>Possible values are:<br><br>- 100 = Organization owner<br>- 200 = Organization administrator<br>- 300 = Organization moderator<br>- 400 = Member<br>- 600 = Guest<br>|
|email|string|false|none|The email address the invitation was sent to. This will not be present when<br>`is_multiuse` is `true` (i.e. the invitation is a reusable invitation link).<br>|
|notify_referrer_on_join|boolean|false|none|A boolean indicating whether the referrer has opted to receive a direct<br>message from [notification bot](/help/configure-automated-notices) when a user<br>account is created using this invitation.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 9.0 (feature level 267). Previously,<br>referrers always received such direct messages.<br>|
|link_url|string|false|none|The URL of the reusable invitation link. This will not be present when<br>`is_multiuse` is `false` (i.e. the invitation is an email invitation).<br>|
|is_multiuse|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the [invitation](/help/invite-new-users) is a<br>reusable invitation link or an email invitation.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|invited_as|100|
|invited_as|200|
|invited_as|300|
|invited_as|400|
|invited_as|600|

<h2 id="tocS_InviteExpirationParameter">InviteExpirationParameter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainviteexpirationparameter"></a>
<a id="schema_InviteExpirationParameter"></a>
<a id="tocSinviteexpirationparameter"></a>
<a id="tocsinviteexpirationparameter"></a>

```json
14400
```

The number of minutes before the invitation will expire. If `null`, the
invitation will never expire. If unspecified, the server will use a default
value (based on the `INVITATION_LINK_VALIDITY_MINUTES` server setting, which
defaults to 14400, i.e. 10 days) for when the invitation will expire.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 6.0 (feature level 126). Previously, there was an
`invite_expires_in_days` parameter, which specified the duration in days instead
of minutes.

<h2 id="tocS_InviteRoleParameter">InviteRoleParameter</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainviteroleparameter"></a>
<a id="schema_InviteRoleParameter"></a>
<a id="tocSinviteroleparameter"></a>
<a id="tocsinviteroleparameter"></a>

```json
600
```

The [organization-level role](/api/roles-and-permissions) of the user that is
created when the invitation is accepted.
Possible values are:

- 100 = Organization owner
- 200 = Organization administrator
- 300 = Organization moderator
- 400 = Member
- 600 = Guest

Users can only create invitation links for
[roles with equal or stricter restrictions](/api/roles-and-permissions#permission-levels)
as their own. For example, a moderator cannot invite someone to be an owner
or administrator, but they can invite them to be a moderator or member.

**Changes**: In Zulip 4.0 (feature level 61), added support for inviting
users as moderators.

```json
  "can_send_message_group": {},

  "can_resolve_topics_group": {},
  "can_create_topic_group": {},
  "is_archived": true,
  "subscriber_count": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_id|integer|false|none|The unique ID of a channel.<br>|
|name|string|false|none|The name of a channel.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|The [description](/help/change-the-channel-description) of the channel in [Zulip-flavored Markdown](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown) format,<br>intended to be used to prepopulate UI for editing a channel's<br>description.<br><br>See [Markdown message formatting](/api/message-formatting) for details on Zulip's HTML format.<br><br>See also `rendered_description`.<br>|
|rendered_description|string|false|none|The [description](/help/change-the-channel-description) of the channel rendered as HTML, intended to<br>be used when displaying the channel description in a UI.<br><br>One should use the standard Zulip rendered_markdown CSS when<br>displaying this content so that emoji, LaTeX, and other syntax<br>work correctly. And any client-side security logic for<br>user-generated message content should be applied when displaying<br>this HTML as though it were the body of a Zulip message.<br><br>See also `description`.<br>|
|date_created|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the channel was created, in UTC seconds.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 30).<br>|
|creator_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the user who created this channel.<br><br>A `null` value means the channel has no recorded creator, which is often<br>because the channel is very old, was created during realm creation or<br>because it was created via a data import tool or [management command][management-commands].<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 9.0 (feature level 254).<br><br>[management-commands]: https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/management-commands.html<br>|
|invite_only|boolean|false|none|Specifies whether the channel is private or not.<br>Only people who have been invited can access a private channel.<br>|
|subscribers|[integer]|false|none|A list of user IDs of users who are also subscribed<br>to a given channel. Included only if `include_subscribers` is `true`.<br>|
|partial_subscribers|[integer]|false|none|If [`include_subscribers="partial"`](/api/get-subscriptions#parameter-include_subscribers)<br>was requested, the server may, at its discretion, send a<br>`partial_subscribers` list rather than a `subscribers` list<br>for channels with a large number of subscribers.<br><br>The `partial_subscribers` list contains an arbitrary<br>subset of the channel's subscribers that is guaranteed<br>to include all bot user subscribers as well as all<br>users who have been active in the last 14 days, but<br>otherwise can be chosen arbitrarily by the server.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 412).<br>|
|desktop_notifications|boolean \| null|false|none|A boolean specifying whether desktop notifications<br>are enabled for the given channel.<br><br>A `null` value means the value of this setting<br>should be inherited from the user-level default<br>setting, `enable_stream_desktop_notifications`, for<br>this channel.<br>|
|email_notifications|boolean \| null|false|none|A boolean specifying whether email notifications<br>are enabled for the given channel.<br><br>A `null` value means the value of this setting<br>should be inherited from the user-level default<br>setting, `enable_stream_email_notifications`, for<br>this channel.<br>|
|wildcard_mentions_notify|boolean \| null|false|none|A boolean specifying whether wildcard mentions<br>trigger notifications as though they were personal<br>mentions in this channel.<br><br>A `null` value means the value of this setting<br>should be inherited from the user-level default<br>setting, wildcard_mentions_notify, for<br>this channel.<br>|
|push_notifications|boolean \| null|false|none|A boolean specifying whether push notifications<br>are enabled for the given channel.<br><br>A `null` value means the value of this setting<br>should be inherited from the user-level default<br>setting, `enable_stream_push_notifications`, for<br>this channel.<br>|
|audible_notifications|boolean \| null|false|none|A boolean specifying whether audible notifications<br>are enabled for the given channel.<br><br>A `null` value means the value of this setting<br>should be inherited from the user-level default<br>setting, `enable_stream_audible_notifications`, for<br>this channel.<br>|
|pin_to_top|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the given channel has been pinned<br>to the top.<br>|
|is_muted|boolean|false|none|Whether the user has muted the channel. Muted channels do<br>not count towards your total unread count and do not show<br>up in the `Combined feed` view (previously known as `All messages`).<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 2.1.0, this feature was<br>represented by the more confusingly named `in_home_view` (with the<br>opposite value, `in_home_view=!is_muted`).<br>|
|in_home_view|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Legacy property for if the given channel is muted, with inverted meaning.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 2.1.0. Clients should use `is_muted`<br>where available.<br>|
|is_announcement_only|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether only organization administrators can post to the channel.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). Clients<br>should use `stream_post_policy` instead.<br>|
|is_web_public|boolean|false|none|Whether the channel has been configured to allow unauthenticated<br>access to its message history from the web.<br>|
|color|string|false|none|The user's personal color for the channel.<br>|
|stream_post_policy|integer|false|none|**Deprecated.** A deprecated representation of a superset of the users who<br>have permission to post messages to the channel available<br>for backwards-compatibility. Clients should use<br>`can_send_message_group` instead.<br><br>It is an enum with the following possible values, corresponding<br>to roles/system groups:<br><br>- 1 = Any user can post.<br>- 2 = Only administrators can post.<br>- 3 = Only [full members][calc-full-member] can post.<br>- 4 = Only moderators can post.<br><br>**Changes**: Deprecated in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 333) and<br>replaced by `can_send_message_group`, which supports finer<br>resolution of configurations, resulting in this property being<br>inaccurate following that transition.<br><br>New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1), replacing the previous<br>`is_announcement_only` boolean.<br><br>[calc-full-member]: /api/roles-and-permissions#determining-if-a-user-is-a-full-member<br>|
|message_retention_days|integer \| null|false|none|Number of days that messages sent to this channel will be stored<br>before being automatically deleted by the [message retention<br>policy](/help/message-retention-policy). There are two special values:<br><br>- `null`, the default, means the channel will inherit the organization<br>  level setting.<br>- `-1` encodes retaining messages in this channel forever.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 17).<br>|
|default_push_notifications|[DefaultPushNotifications](#schemadefaultpushnotifications)|false|none|Whether mobile push notifications will be enabled by default when a<br>user first subscribes to this channel, potentially overriding the<br>user's [default mobile notification<br>setting](/help/channel-notifications#configure-default-notifications-for-all-channels)<br>for channel messages.<br><br>Because this default is applied only the first time a user<br>subscribes, unsubscribing and resubscribing a user does not reset<br>their preference to this channel default.<br><br>Only organization administrators can set or modify this value.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 13.0 (feature level 507).<br>|
|history_public_to_subscribers|boolean|false|none|Whether the history of the channel is public to its subscribers.<br><br>Currently always true for public channels (i.e. `"invite_only": false` implies<br>`"history_public_to_subscribers": true`), but clients should not make that<br>assumption, as we may change that behavior in the future.<br>|
|first_message_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the first message in the channel.<br><br>Intended to help clients determine whether they need to display<br>UI like the "show all topics" widget that would suggest the channel<br>has older history that can be accessed.<br><br>Is `null` for channels with no message history.<br>|
|folder_id|[FolderId](#schemafolderid)|false|none|The ID of the folder to which the channel belongs.<br><br>Is `null` if channel does not belong to any folder.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 389).<br>|
|topics_policy|[TopicsPolicy](#schematopicspolicy)|false|none|Whether [named topics](/help/introduction-to-topics) and the empty<br>topic (i.e., ["general chat" topic](/help/general-chat-topic))<br>are enabled in this channel.<br><br>- `"inherit"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this channel,<br>  and the [organization-level `realm_topics_policy`][realm-topics-policy]<br>  is used for whether messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel.<br>- `"allow_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to both named topics and<br>  the empty topic in this channel.<br>- `"disable_empty_topic"`: Messages can be sent to named topics in this<br>  channel, but the empty topic is disabled.<br>- `"empty_topic_only"`: Messages can be sent to the empty topic in this<br>  channel, but named topics are disabled. See ["general chat"<br>  channels](/help/general-chat-channels).<br><br>The `"empty_topic_only"` policy can only be set if all existing messages<br>in the channel are already in the empty topic.<br><br>When creating a new channel, if the `topics_policy` is not specified, the<br>`"inherit"` option will be set.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 11.0 (feature level 404), the `"empty_topic_only"`<br>option was added.<br><br>New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 392).<br><br>[realm-topics-policy]: /help/require-topics#set-the-default-general-chat-topic-configuration<br>|
|is_recently_active|boolean|false|none|Whether the channel has recent message activity. Clients should use this to implement<br>[hiding inactive channels](/help/manage-inactive-channels).<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 323). Previously, clients implemented the<br>demote_inactive_streams from local message history, resulting in a choppy loading<br>experience.<br>|
|stream_weekly_traffic|integer \| null|false|none|The average number of messages sent to the channel per week, as<br>estimated based on recent weeks, rounded to the nearest integer.<br><br>If `null`, the channel was recently created and there is<br>insufficient data to estimate the average traffic.<br>|
|can_add_subscribers_group|[ChannelCanAddSubscribersGroup](#schemachannelcanaddsubscribersgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_remove_subscribers_group|[CanRemoveSubscribersGroup](#schemacanremovesubscribersgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_administer_channel_group|[CanAdministerChannelGroup](#schemacanadministerchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_delete_any_message_group|[CanDeleteAnyMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteanymessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_delete_own_message_group|[CanDeleteOwnMessageGroup](#schemacandeleteownmessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_move_messages_out_of_channel_group|[CanMoveMessagesOutOfChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessagesoutofchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_move_messages_within_channel_group|[CanMoveMessagesWithinChannelGroup](#schemacanmovemessageswithinchannelgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_send_message_group|[CanSendMessageGroup](#schemacansendmessagegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_subscribe_group|[CanSubscribeGroup](#schemacansubscribegroup)|false|none|none|
|can_resolve_topics_group|[CanResolveTopicsGroup](#schemacanresolvetopicsgroup)|false|none|none|
|can_create_topic_group|[CanCreateTopicGroup](#schemacancreatetopicgroup)|false|none|none|
|is_archived|boolean|false|none|A boolean indicating whether the channel is [archived](/help/archive-a-channel).<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 315).<br>Previously, subscriptions only included active<br>channels. Note that some endpoints will never return archived<br>channels unless the client declares explicit support for<br>them via the `archived_channels` client capability.<br>|
|subscriber_count|number|false|none|The total number of non-deactivated users (including bots) who<br>are subscribed to the channel. Clients are responsible for updating<br>this value using `peer_add` and `peer_remove` events.<br><br>The server's internals cannot guarantee this value is correctly<br>synced with `peer_add` and `peer_remove` events for the channel. As<br>a result, if a (rare) race occurs between a change in the channel's<br>subscribers and fetching this value, it is possible for a client<br>that is correctly following the events protocol to end up with a<br>permanently off-by-one error in the channel's subscriber count.<br><br>Clients are recommended to fetch full subscriber data for a channel<br>in contexts where it is important to avoid this risk. The official<br>web application, for example, uses this field primarily while<br>waiting to fetch a given channel's full subscriber list from the<br>server.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 394).<br>|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|topics_policy|inherit|
|topics_policy|allow_empty_topic|
|topics_policy|disable_empty_topic|
|topics_policy|empty_topic_only|

<h2 id="tocS_EmailAddressVisibility">EmailAddressVisibility</h2>

<a id="tocsemailaddressvisibility"></a>

```json
0
```

The [policy][permission-level] for [which other users][help-email-visibility]
in this organization can see the user's real email address.

- 1 = Everyone
- 2 = Members only
- 3 = Administrators only
- 4 = Nobody
- 5 = Moderators only

**Changes**: New in Zulip 7.0 (feature level 163), replacing the
realm-level setting.

[permission-level]: /api/roles-and-permissions#permission-levels
[help-email-visibility]: /help/configure-email-visibility

|emoji_name|object|false|none|none|
|reaction_type|object|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|avatar_url|string \| null|false|none|The URL of the message sender's avatar. Can be `null` only if<br>the current user has access to the sender's real email address<br>and `client_gravatar` was `true`.<br><br>If `null`, then the sender has not uploaded an avatar in Zulip,<br>and the client can compute the gravatar URL by hashing the<br>sender's email address, which corresponds in this case to their<br>real email address.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 7.0 (feature level 163), access to a<br>user's real email address was a realm-level setting. As of this<br>feature level, `email_address_visibility` is a user setting.<br>|
|client|string|false|none|A Zulip "client" string, describing what Zulip client<br>sent the message.<br>|
|content|string|false|none|The content/body of the message.<br>When `apply_markdown` is set, it will be in HTML format.<br><br>See [Markdown message formatting](/api/message-formatting) for details on Zulip's HTML format.<br>|
|content_type|string|false|none|The HTTP `content_type` for the message content. This<br>will be `text/html` or `text/x-markdown`, depending on<br>whether `apply_markdown` was set.<br><br>See the help center article on [message formatting](/help/format-your-message-using-markdown) for details on Zulip-flavored Markdown.<br>|
|display_recipient|string \| [object]|false|none|Data on the recipient of the message. Will be one of the following:<br>|
|edit_history|[object]|false|none|An array of objects, with each object documenting the<br>changes in a previous edit made to the message,<br>ordered chronologically from most recent to least recent<br>edit.<br><br>Not present if the message has never been edited or moved,<br>or if [viewing message edit history][edit-history-access]<br>is not allowed in the organization.<br><br>Every object will contain `user_id` and `timestamp`.<br><br>The other fields are optional, and will be present or not<br>depending on whether the channel, topic, and/or message<br>content were modified in the edit event. For example, if<br>only the topic was edited, only `prev_topic` and `topic`<br>will be present in addition to `user_id` and `timestamp`.<br><br>[edit-history-access]: /help/restrict-message-edit-history-access<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 10.0 (feature level 284), removed the<br>`prev_rendered_content_version` field as it is an internal<br>server implementation detail not used by any client.<br>|
|id|integer|false|none|The unique message ID. Messages should always be<br>displayed sorted by ID.<br>|
|is_me_message|boolean|false|none|Whether the message is a [/me status message][status-messages]<br><br>[status-messages]: /help/format-your-message-using-markdown#status-messages<br>|
|last_edit_timestamp|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the message's content was last edited, in<br>UTC seconds.<br><br>Not present if the message's content has never been edited.<br><br>Clients should use this field, rather than parsing the `edit_history`<br>array, to display an indicator that the message has been edited.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 10.0 (feature level 365), this was the<br>time when the message was last edited or moved.<br>|
|last_moved_timestamp|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the message was last moved to a different<br>channel or topic, in UTC seconds.<br><br>Not present if the message has never been moved, or if the only topic<br>moves for the message are [resolving or unresolving](/help/resolve-a-topic)<br>the message's topic.<br><br>Clients should use this field, rather than parsing the `edit_history`<br>array, to display an indicator that the message has been moved.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 365). Previously,<br>parsing the `edit_history` array was required in order to correctly<br>display moved message indicators.<br>|
|reactions|[[EmojiReaction](#schemaemojireaction)]|false|none|Data on any [reactions](/help/emoji-reactions) to the message,<br>ordered chronologically from oldest to newest reaction.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 10.0 (feature level 328), the deprecated `user`<br>object was removed from the data for each reaction. It contained the<br>following information about the user who added the reaction: `id`,<br>`email`, `full_name` and `is_mirror_dummy`.<br>|
|recipient_id|integer|false|none|A unique ID for the set of users receiving the<br>message (either a channel or group of users). Useful primarily<br>for hashing.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 12.0 (feature level 482),<br>`recipient_id` in 1:1 direct messages changed to a new<br>value; it still has the semantics of "the 1:1 conversation<br>with a specific user," but the raw value changed due to<br>internal changes.<br><br>Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 327), `recipient_id`<br>was the same across all incoming 1:1 direct messages. Now, each<br>incoming message uniquely shares a `recipient_id` with outgoing<br>messages in the same conversation.<br>|
|sender_email|string|false|none|The Zulip API email address of the message's sender.<br>|
|sender_full_name|string|false|none|The full name of the message's sender.<br>|
|sender_id|integer|false|none|The user ID of the message's sender.<br>|
|sender_realm_str|string|false|none|A string identifier for the realm the sender is in. Unique only within<br>the context of a given Zulip server.<br><br>E.g. on `example.zulip.com`, this will be `example`.<br>|
|stream_id|integer|false|none|Only present for channel messages; the ID of the channel.<br>|
|subject|string|false|none|The `topic` of the message. Currently always `""` for direct messages,<br>though this could change if Zulip adds support for topics in direct<br>message conversations.<br><br>The field name is a legacy holdover from when topics were<br>called "subjects" and will eventually change.<br><br>For clients that don't support the `empty_topic_name` [client capability][client-capabilities],<br>the empty string value is replaced with the value of `realm_empty_topic_display_name`<br>found in the [POST /register](/api/register-queue) response, for channel messages.<br><br>**Changes**: Before Zulip 10.0 (feature level 334), `empty_topic_name`<br>client capability didn't exist and empty string as the topic name for<br>channel messages wasn't allowed.<br><br>[client-capabilities]: /api/register-queue#parameter-client_capabilities<br>|
|submessages|[object]|false|none|Data used for certain experimental Zulip integrations.<br>|
|timestamp|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the message was sent,<br>in UTC seconds.<br>|
|topic_links|[object]|false|none|Data on any links to be included in the `topic`<br>line (these are generated by [custom linkification<br>filters](/help/add-a-custom-linkifier) that match content in the<br>message's topic.)<br><br>**Changes**: This field contained a list of urls before<br>Zulip 4.0 (feature level 46).<br><br>New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). Previously, this field was called<br>`subject_links`; clients are recommended to rename `subject_links` to `topic_links`<br>if present for compatibility with older Zulip servers.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the message: `"stream"` or `"private"`.<br>|
|avatar_url|object \| null|false|none|none|
|client|object|false|none|none|
|content|object|false|none|none|
|content_type|object|false|none|none|
|display_recipient|object|false|none|none|

Previously, this field was called<br>`subject_links`; clients are recommended to rename `subject_links` to `topic_links`<br>if present for compatibility with older Zulip servers.<br>|
|type|string|false|none|The type of the message: `"stream"` or `"private"`.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_ModernPresenceFormat">ModernPresenceFormat</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamodernpresenceformat"></a>
<a id="schema_ModernPresenceFormat"></a>
<a id="tocSmodernpresenceformat"></a>
<a id="tocsmodernpresenceformat"></a>

```json
{
  "active_timestamp": 0,
  "idle_timestamp": 0
}
```

`{user_id}`: Presence data (modern format) for the user with
the specified ID.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active_timestamp|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp of the last time a client connected<br>to Zulip reported that the user was actually present<br>(e.g. via focusing a browser window or interacting<br>with a computer running the desktop app).<br><br>Clients should display users with a current<br>`active_timestamp` as fully present.<br>|
|idle_timestamp|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp of the last time the user had a<br>client connected to Zulip, including idle clients<br>where the user hasn't interacted with the system<br>recently.<br><br>The Zulip server has no way of distinguishing whether<br>an idle web app user is at their computer, but hasn't<br>interacted with the Zulip tab recently, or simply left<br>their desktop computer on when they left.<br><br>Thus, clients should display users with a current<br>`idle_timestamp` but no current `active_timestamp` as<br>potentially present.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_LegacyPresenceFormat">LegacyPresenceFormat</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemalegacypresenceformat"></a>
<a id="schema_LegacyPresenceFormat"></a>
<a id="tocSlegacypresenceformat"></a>
<a id="tocslegacypresenceformat"></a>

```json
{
  "client": "string",
  "status": "idle",
  "timestamp": 0,
  "pushable": true
}
```

`{client_name}` or `"aggregated"`: Object containing the details of the user's
presence.

**Changes**: Starting with Zulip 7.0 (feature level 178), this will always
contain two keys, `"website"` and `"aggregated"`, with identical data. The
server no longer stores which client submitted presence updates.

Previously, the `{client_name}` keys for these objects were the names of the
different clients where the user was logged in, for example `website` or
`ZulipDesktop`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client|string|false|none|The client's platform name.<br><br>**Changes**: Starting with Zulip 7.0 (feature level 178), this will<br>always be `"website"` as the server no longer stores which client<br>submitted presence data.<br>|
|status|string|false|none|The status of the user on this client. Will be either `"idle"`<br>or `"active"`.<br>|
|timestamp|integer|false|none|The UNIX timestamp of when this client sent the user's presence<br>to the server with the precision of a second.<br>|
|pushable|boolean|false|none|Whether the client is capable of showing mobile/push notifications<br>to the user.<br><br>Not present in objects with the `"aggregated"` key.<br><br>**Changes**: Starting with Zulip 7.0 (feature level 178), always<br>`false` when present as the server no longer stores which client<br>submitted presence data.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|idle|
|status|active|

To be removed in a future release.<br>|

Each emoji<br>`reaction_type` has an independent namespace for values of `emoji_code`.<br><br>Must be one of the following values:<br><br>- `unicode_emoji` : In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be a<br>  dash-separated hex encoding of the sequence of Unicode codepoints<br>  that define this emoji in the Unicode specification.<br><br>- `realm_emoji` : In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be the ID of<br>  the uploaded [custom emoji](/help/custom-emoji).<br><br>- `zulip_extra_emoji` : These are special emoji included with Zulip.<br>  In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be the name of the emoji (e.g.<br>  "zulip").<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 5.0 (feature level 86).<br>|

Represents a user's personal configuration for a specific
navigation view (displayed most visibly at the top of the web
application's left sidebar).

Navigation views can be either an override to the default
behavior of a built-in view, or a custom view.

**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 390).

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|is_pinned|boolean|true|none|Determines whether the view appears directly in the sidebar or<br>is hidden in the "More Views" menu.<br><br>- `true` - Pinned and visible in the sidebar.<br>- `false` - Hidden and accessible via the "More Views" menu.<br>|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The user-facing name for custom navigation views. Omit this<br>field for built-in views.<br>|

```json
{
  "require_system_group": true,
  "allow_internet_group": true,
  "allow_nobody_group": true,
  "allow_everyone_group": true,
  "default_group_name": "string",
  "default_for_system_groups": "string",
  "allowed_system_groups": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Configuration for a group permission setting specifying the groups
to which the setting can be set to and the default values for the
setting.

**Changes**: Removed `allow_owners_group` field in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 326), as we now
support anonymous user groups. Previously, the `role:owners` system group was
not offered when `allow_owners_group` was false.

Removed unnecessary `id_field_name` field in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 326). Previously,
this always had the value of `"{setting_name}_id"`; it was an internal implementation
detail of the server not intended to be included in the API.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|require_system_group|boolean|false|none|Whether the setting can only be set to a system user group.<br>|
|allow_internet_group|boolean|false|none|Whether the setting can be set to `role:internet` system group.<br>|
|allow_nobody_group|boolean|false|none|Whether the setting can be set to `role:nobody` system group.<br>|
|allow_everyone_group|boolean|false|none|Whether the setting can be set to `role:everyone` system group.<br><br>If false, guest users cannot exercise this permission even if they are part of<br>the [group-setting value](/api/group-setting-values) for this setting.<br>|
|default_group_name|string|false|none|Name of the default system group for the setting.<br><br>For some group settings, this can be `"group_creator"`. In that<br>case, the default for the setting is an anonymous group whose<br>only member is the group's creator.<br><br>For some channel settings, this can be `"channel_creator"`.<br>In that case:<br><br>- If the channel's [`creator_id`][channel-response] is not `null`, default for the<br>  setting is an anonymous group with the channel creator as<br>  the only member.<br>- If the channel's [`creator_id`][channel-response] is `null`, default for the setting<br>  is `role:nobody` system group.<br><br>**Changes**: In Zulip 12.0 (feature level 427), renamed<br>`"stream_creator_or_nobody"` value to `"channel_creator"`.<br><br>[channel-response]: /api/get-stream-by-id#response<br>|
|default_for_system_groups|string \| null|false|none|Name of the default group for the setting for system groups.<br><br>This is non-null only for group-level settings.<br>|
|allowed_system_groups|[string]|false|none|An array of names of system groups to which the setting can<br>be set to.<br><br>If the list is empty, the setting can be set to system groups<br>based on the other boolean fields.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 8.0 (feature level 225).<br>|

In previous<br>versions, there was a `bot_owner` field containing the email<br>address of the bot's owner.<br>|
|role|integer|false|none|[Organization-level role](/api/roles-and-permissions) of the user.<br>Possible values are:<br><br>- 100 = Organization owner<br>- 200 = Organization administrator<br>- 300 = Organization moderator<br>- 400 = Member<br>- 600 = Guest<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 59).<br>|

```json
{
  "user_id": 0,
  "delivery_email": "string",
  "email": "string",
  "full_name": "string",
  "date_joined": "string",
  "is_active": true,
  "is_owner": true,
  "is_admin": true,
  "is_guest": true,
  "is_bot": true,
  "bot_type": 0,
  "bot_owner_id": 0,
  "role": 100,

```

A dictionary containing basic data on a given Zulip user.

**Changes**: Removed `is_billing_admin` field in Zulip 10.0 (feature level 363), as it was
replaced by the `can_manage_billing_group` realm setting.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|integer|false|none|The unique ID of the user.<br>|
|delivery_email|string \| null|false|none|The user's real email address. This value will be `null` if you cannot<br>access user's real email address. For bot users, this field is always<br>set to the real email of the bot, because bot users always have<br>`email_address_visibility` set to everyone.<br><br>**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 7.0 (feature level 163), this field was<br>present only when `email_address_visibility` was restricted and you had<br>access to the user's real email. As of this feature level, this field<br>is always present, including the case when `email_address_visibility`<br>is set to everyone (and therefore not restricted).<br>|
|email|string|false|none|The Zulip API email address of the user or bot.<br><br>If you do not have permission to view the email address of the target user,<br>this will be a fake email address that is usable for the Zulip API but nothing else.<br>|
|full_name|string|false|none|Full name of the user or bot, used for all display purposes.<br>|
|date_joined|string|false|none|The time when the user joined. For users imported from other<br>applications and users created via the API, this is set to the<br>account creation time until the user logs in for the first time,<br>after which it is updated to that login time.<br><br>For imported users, clients can use the `is_imported_stub` flag<br>to determine how to display this field: when `is_imported_stub`<br>is `true`, the user has not yet logged in and this value is the<br>account creation time during import; when `is_imported_stub` is<br>`false`, this value reflects when the user first logged in.<br><br>**Changes**: Starting with Zulip 12.0 (feature level 475),<br>this field is updated when an imported stub user or a user created<br>via the API logs in for the first time.<br>|
|is_active|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user account has been deactivated.<br>|
|is_owner|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user is an organization owner.<br>If true, `is_admin` will also be true.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 8).<br>|
|is_admin|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user is an organization administrator.<br>|
|is_guest|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user is a guest user.<br>|
|is_bot|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user is a bot or full account.<br>|
|bot_type|integer \| null|false|none|An integer describing the type of bot:<br><br>- `null` if the user isn't a bot.<br>- `1` for a `Generic` bot.<br>- `2` for an `Incoming webhook` bot.<br>- `3` for an `Outgoing webhook` bot.<br>- `4` for an `Embedded` bot.<br>|
|bot_owner_id|integer \| null|false|none|If the user is a bot (i.e. `is_bot` is true), then `bot_owner_id`<br>is the user ID of the bot's owner (usually, whoever created the bot).<br><br>Will be `null` for legacy bots that do not have an owner.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 1). In previous<br>versions, there was a `bot_owner` field containing the email<br>address of the bot's owner.<br>|
|role|integer|false|none|[Organization-level role](/api/roles-and-permissions) of the user.<br>Possible values are:<br><br>- 100 = Organization owner<br>- 200 = Organization administrator<br>- 300 = Organization moderator<br>- 400 = Member<br>- 600 = Guest<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 4.0 (feature level 59).<br>|
|timezone|string|false|none|The IANA identifier of the user's [profile time zone](/help/change-your-timezone),<br>which is used primarily to display the user's local time to other users.<br>|

As of this<br>feature level, `email_address_visibility` is a user setting.<br><br>In Zulip 3.0 (feature level 18), if the client has the<br>`user_avatar_url_field_optional` capability, this will be missing at<br>the server's sole discretion.<br>|

|is_imported_stub|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this user object is a stub account imported from<br>another chat system. Stub accounts are used to represent the senders<br>for imported messages. Stub accounts can be converted to regular Zulip<br>accounts when the user starts using Zulip, preserving that imported<br>user's message history.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 12.0 (feature level 433).<br>|
|is_deleted|boolean|false|none|A boolean specifying whether the user has been permanently<br>deleted. <h2 id="tocS_ProfileData">ProfileData</h2>

```json
  "property1": {
    "value": "string",
    "rendered_value": "string"
  },
  "property2": {
    "value": "string",
    "rendered_value": "string"
  }
}
```

Only present if `is_bot` is false; bots can't have custom profile fields.

A dictionary containing custom profile field data for the user. Each entry
maps the integer ID of a custom profile field in the organization to a
dictionary containing the user's data for that field. Generally the data
includes just a single `value` key; for those custom profile fields
supporting Markdown, a `rendered_value` key will also be present.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|`{id}`: Object with data about what value the user filled in the custom<br>profile field with that ID.<br>|

### Properties

|id|integer|false|none|The unique ID of the channel folder.<br>|

|order|integer|false|none|This value determines in which order the channel folder should be<br>displayed in the UI. The value is 0 indexed, and a channel folder with<br>a lower value should be displayed before channel folders with higher<br>values.<br><br>**Changes**: New in Zulip 11.0 (feature level 414).<br>|
|date_created|integer \| null|false|none|The UNIX timestamp for when the channel folder was created,<br>in UTC seconds.<br>|
|creator_id|integer \| null|false|none|The ID of the user who created the channel folder.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|The description of the channel folder. Can be an empty string.<br><br>See [Markdown message formatting](/api/message-formatting) for details<br>on Zulip's HTML format.<br>|
|rendered_description|string|false|none|The description of the channel folder rendered as HTML, intended to be<br>used for UI that displays the channel folder description.<br><br>Clients should use the standard Zulip rendered_markdown CSS when<br>displaying this content so that emoji, LaTeX, and other syntax work<br>correctly. And any client-side security logic for user-generated<br>message content should be applied when displaying this HTML as though<br>it were the body of a Zulip message.<br>|
|is_archived|boolean|false|none|Whether the channel folder is archived or not.<br>|

(feature level 78) as a return value for the

<h2 id="tocS_Event_types">Event_types</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaevent_types"></a>
<a id="schema_Event_types"></a>
<a id="tocSevent_types"></a>
<a id="tocsevent_types"></a>

```json
[
  "message"
]
```

A JSON-encoded array indicating which types of events you're interested
in. Values that you might find useful include:

- **message** (messages)
- **subscription** (changes in your subscriptions)
- **realm_user** (changes to users in the organization and
  their properties, such as their name).

If you do not specify this parameter, you will receive all
events, and have to filter out the events not relevant to
your client in your client code. For most applications, one
is only interested in messages, so one specifies:
`"event_types": ["message"]`

Event types not supported by the server are ignored, in order to simplify
the implementation of client apps that support multiple server versions.

<h2 id="tocS_Narrow">Narrow</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanarrow"></a>
<a id="schema_Narrow"></a>
<a id="tocSnarrow"></a>
<a id="tocsnarrow"></a>

```json
[
  [
    "channel",
    "Denmark"
  ]
]
```

A JSON-encoded array of arrays of length 2 indicating the
[narrow filter(s)](/api/construct-narrow) for which you'd
like to receive events for.

For example, to receive events for direct messages (including
group direct messages) received by the user, one can use
`"narrow": [["is", "dm"]]`.

Unlike the API for [fetching messages](/api/get-messages),
this narrow parameter is simply a filter on messages that the
user receives through their channel subscriptions (or because
they are a recipient of a direct message).

This means that a client that requests a `narrow` filter of
`[["channel", "Denmark"]]` will receive events for new messages
sent to that channel while the user is subscribed to that
channel. The client will not receive any message events at all
if the user is not subscribed to `"Denmark"`.

Newly created bot users are not usually subscribed to any
channels, so bots using this API need to be
[subscribed](/api/subscribe) to any channels whose messages
you'd like them to process using this endpoint.

See the `all_public_streams` parameter for how to process all
public channel messages in an organization.

**Changes**: See [changes section](/api/construct-narrow#changes)
of search/narrow filter documentation.

<h2 id="tocS_ReactionType">ReactionType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareactiontype"></a>
<a id="schema_ReactionType"></a>
<a id="tocSreactiontype"></a>
<a id="tocsreactiontype"></a>

```json
"unicode_emoji"
```

A string indicating the type of emoji. Each emoji `reaction_type`
has an independent namespace for values of `emoji_code`.

If an API client is adding/removing a vote on an existing reaction,
it should pass this parameter using the value the server provided
for the existing reaction for specificity. Supported values:

- `unicode_emoji` : In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be a
  dash-separated hex encoding of the sequence of Unicode codepoints
  that define this emoji in the Unicode specification.

- `realm_emoji` : In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be the ID of
  the uploaded [custom emoji](/help/custom-emoji).

- `zulip_extra_emoji` : These are special emoji included with Zulip.
  In this namespace, `emoji_code` will be the name of the emoji (e.g.
  "zulip").

**Changes**: In Zulip 3.0 (feature level 2), this parameter became
optional for [custom emoji](/help/custom-emoji);
previously, this endpoint assumed `unicode_emoji` if this
parameter was not specified.

<h2 id="tocS_EmojiCode">EmojiCode</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemojicode"></a>
<a id="schema_EmojiCode"></a>
<a id="tocSemojicode"></a>
<a id="tocsemojicode"></a>

```json
"1f419"
```

A unique identifier, defining the specific emoji codepoint requested,
within the namespace of the `reaction_type`.

For most API clients, you won't need this, but it's important
for Zulip apps to handle rare corner cases when
adding/removing votes on an emoji reaction added previously by
another user.

If the existing reaction was added when the Zulip server was
using a previous version of the emoji data mapping between
Unicode codepoints and human-readable names, sending the
`emoji_code` in the data for the original reaction allows the
Zulip server to correctly interpret your upvote as an upvote
rather than a reaction with a "different" emoji.

<h2 id="tocS_MessageRetentionDays">MessageRetentionDays</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamessageretentiondays"></a>
<a id="schema_MessageRetentionDays"></a>
<a id="tocSmessageretentiondays"></a>
<a id="tocsmessageretentiondays"></a>

```json
"20"
```

Number of days that messages sent to this channel will be stored
before being automatically deleted by the [message retention
policy](/help/message-retention-policy). Two special string format
values are supported:

- `"realm_default"`: Return to the organization-level setting.
- `"unlimited"`: Retain messages forever.

**Changes**: Prior to Zulip 5.0 (feature level 91), retaining
messages forever was encoded using `"forever"` instead of
`"unlimited"`.

New in Zulip 3.0 (feature level 17).
